passages.text:
It is curious that Stephen Koziatek feels almost as though he has to justify his efforts to give his students a better future.

Mr. Koziatek is part of something pioneering. He is a teacher at a New Hampshire high school where learning is not something of books and tests and mechanical memorization, but practical. When did it become accepted wisdom that students should be able to name the 13th president of the United States but be utterly overwhelmed by a broken bike chain?

As Koziatek knows, there is learning in just about everything. Nothing is necessarily gained by forcing students to learn geometry at a graffitied desk stuck with generations of discarded chewing gum. They can also learn geometry by assembling a bicycle.

But he's also found a kind of insidious prejudice. Working with your hands is seen as almost a mark of inferiority. Schools in the family of vocational education "have that stereotype…that it's for kids who can't make it academically," he says.

On one hand, that viewpoint is a logical product of America's evolution. Manufacturing is not the economic engine that it once was. The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated. More education is the new principle. We want more for our kids, and rightfully so.

But the headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all – and the subtle devaluing of anything less – misses an important point: That's not the only thing the American economy needs. Yes, a bachelor's degree opens more doors. But even now, 54 percent of the jobs in the country are middle-skill jobs, such as construction and high-skill manufacturing. But only 44 percent of workers are adequately trained.

In other words, at a time when the working class has turned the country on its political head, frustrated that the opportunity that once defined America is vanishing, one obvious solution is staring us in the face. There is a gap in working-class jobs, but the workers who need those jobs most aren't equipped to do them. Koziatek's Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap.

Koziatek's school is a wake-up call. When education becomes one-size-fits-all, it risks overlooking a nation's diversity of gifts.

A new survey by Harvard University finds more than two-thirds of young Americans disapprove of President Trump's use of Twitter. The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president's social media platform.

Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines. Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills. Such a trend is badly needed. During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford. And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant.

Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace. A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use "distributed trust" to verify stories. They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives – especially those that are open about any bias. "Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints," the survey concluded.

Such active research can have another effect. A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people's reliance on social media led to greater political engagement.

Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests. This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information. A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is "reader error," more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting. About a third say the problem of fake news lies in "misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news" via social media. In other words, the choice to share news on social media may be the heart of the issue. "This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem," says Roxanne Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group.

So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills – and in their choices on when to share on social media.

passages.text:
While fossil fuels – coal, oil, gas – still generate roughly 85 percent of the world's energy supply, it's clearer than ever that the future belongs to renewable sources such as wind and solar. The move to renewables is picking up momentum around the world: They now account for more than half of new power sources going on line.

Some growth stems from a commitment by governments and farsighted businesses to fund cleaner energy sources. But increasingly the story is about the plummeting prices of renewables, especially wind and solar. The cost of solar panels has dropped by 80 percent and the cost of wind turbines by close to one-third in the past eight years.

In many parts of the world renewable energy is already a principal energy source. In Scotland, for example, wind turbines provide enough electricity to power 95 percent of homes. While the rest of the world takes the lead, notably China and Europe, the United States is also seeing a remarkable shift. In March, for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent of the power generated in the US, reported the US Energy Information Administration.

President Trump has underlined fossil fuels – especially coal – as the path to economic growth. In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source. But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation – and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers.

The question "what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely.

The advance is driven in part by vehicle manufacturers, who are placing big bets on battery-powered electric vehicles. Although electric cars are still a rarity on roads now, this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years.

While there's a long way to go, the trend lines for renewables are spiking. The pace of change in energy sources appears to be speeding up – perhaps just in time to have a meaningful effect in slowing climate change. What Washington does – or doesn't do – to promote alternative energy may mean less and less at a time of a global shift in thought.

passages.text:
Any fair-minded assessment of the dangers of the deal between Britain's National Health Service (NHS) and DeepMind must start by acknowledging that both sides mean well. DeepMind is one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) companies in the world. The potential of this work applied to healthcare is very great, but it could also lead to further concentration of power in the tech giants. It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 on the basis of a vague agreement which took far too little account of the patients' rights and their expectations of privacy.

DeepMind has almost apologized. The NHS trust has mended its ways. Further arrangements – and there may be many – between the NHS and DeepMind will be carefully scrutinised to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn. But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it. But this distinction misses the point that it is processing and aggregation, not the mere possession of bits, that gives the data value.

The great question is who should benefit from the analysis of all the data that our lives now generate. Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them. That misses the way the surveillance economy works. The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.

The use of privacy law to curb the tech giants in this instance feels slightly maladapted. This practice does not address the real worry. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that they will belong to a private monopoly which developed them using public resources. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed to avoid a future of digital feudalism. Ms Denham's report is a welcome start.

passages.text:
The power and ambition of the giants of the digital economy are astonishing—Amazon has just announced the purchase of the upmarket grocery chain Whole Foods for ＄ 13.5bn, but two years ago Facebook paid even more than that to acquire the WhatsApp messaging service, which doesn't have any physical product at all. What WhatsApp offered Facebook was an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives.

Facebook promised the European commission then that it would not link phone numbers to Facebook identities, but it broke the promise almost as soon as the deal went through. Even without knowing what was in the messages, the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be. What political journalist, what party whip, would not want to know the makeup of the WhatsApp groups in which Theresa May's enemies are currently plotting? It may be that the value of Whole Foods to Amazon is not so much the 460 shops it owns, but the records of which customers have purchased what.

Competition law appears to be the only way to address these imbalances of power. But it is clumsy. For one thing, it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy. By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace, to be replaced by new abuses of power. But there is a deeper conceptual problem, too. Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them. The users of their services are not their customers. That would be the people who buy advertising from them – and Facebook and Google, the two virtual giants, dominate digital advertising to the disadvantage of all other media and entertainment companies.

The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants. Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield. Ants keep predatory insects away from where their aphids feed; Gmail keeps the spammers out of our inboxes. It doesn't feel like a human or democratic relationship, even if both sides benefit.

passages.text:
The U.S. Postal Service (USPS) continues to bleed red ink. It reported a net loss of $5.6 billion for fiscal 2016, the 10th straight year its expenses have exceeded revenue. Meanwhile, it has more than $120 billion in unfunded liabilities, mostly for employee health and retirement costs. There are many reasons this formerly stable federal institution finds itself at the brink of bankruptcy. Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and a regulatory structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality.

And interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers exert self-interested pressure on the USPS's ultimate overseer – Congress – insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. This is why repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization.

Now comes word that everyone involved – Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system's heaviest users – has finally agreed on a plan to fix the system. Legislation is moving through the House that would save USPS an estimated $28.6 billion over five years, which could help pay for new vehicles, among other survival measures. Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. The latter step would largely offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care, thus addressing a long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions.

If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate – where someone is bound to point out that it amounts to the bare, bare minimum necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, not comprehensive reform. There's no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of the agency's costs. Also missing is any discussion of eliminating Saturday letter delivery. That common-sense change enjoys wide public support and would save the USPS $2 billion per year. But postal special-interest groups seem to have killed it, at least in the House. The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that legislators are getting frightened about a politically embarrassing short-term collapse at the USPS. It is not, however, a sign that they're getting serious about transforming the postal system for the 21st century.

passages.text:
To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of "deep work" – the ability to focus without distraction.

There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work – be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day. Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.

Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time. "At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month. Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor's appointment or important meeting", he writes.

Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritise your day – in particular how we craft our to-do lists. Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day.

While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students. Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results.

In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, "be lazy".

"Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body…[idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done," he argues.

Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate. When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.

"What people don't realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain," says Pillay.

questions.content: What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?

questions.content: It can be learned that in Iowa, ____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "wind is a widely used energy source", "B": "wind energy has replaced fossil fuels", "C": "tech giants are investing in clean energy", "D": "there is a shortage of clean energy supply"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation ↔ wind is a widely used energy source 预判 \"风电在爱荷华广泛使用\" 与 wind is a widely used energy source 在主体、范 围、性质三方面完全对位。"},"B":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"原文只说风电占 36% 发电量，化石能源剩余 64% 仍可能存在；wind energy has replaced fossil fuels 中的 replaced（已替代）大大超出原文事实。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文是科技巨头 being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers——他们 \"被清洁能源吸引来建数据中心\"，主体是被吸引来用电，不是 \"投资清洁能源\"。tech giants are investing in clean energy 偷换为 \"投资清洁能源\"。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文 the availability of clean energy 明示清洁能源 \"充足可用\"；there is a shortage of clean energy supply 表达 \"清洁能源短缺\"，与原文方向完全相反。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：It can be learned that in Iowa, ____. 虽含 be learned，但配套限定 in Iowa 把范围收死在 一个具体地点的客观事实上，仍属细节题而非推断题。","拆句：It can be learned that in Iowa, ____. 是形式主语 it 引导的复合句，that 后是不完整陈述 句，in Iowa 是地点状语，主语谓语缺失由选项补全；无复杂结构。","定位：But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation – and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers. 但这一说法在爱荷华州并不受欢迎——那里风电机组遍布田野，提供该州 36% 的发电量； 微软这样的科技巨头也因清洁能源充足而被吸引来建数据中心。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第47—60页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation – and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第1—633页；原文定位：But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation – and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers. 但这一说法在爱荷华州并不受欢迎——那里风电机组遍布田野，提供该州 36% 的发电量； 微软这样的科技巨头也因清洁能源充足而被吸引来建数据中心。

questions.content: Which of the following is true about clean energy according to Paragraphs 5&6?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Its application has boosted battery storage.", "B": "It is commonly used in car manufacturing.", "C": "Its continuous supply is becoming a reality.", "D": "Its sustainable exploitation will remain difficult."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文 a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely 中，是电池储能提升 → 推动清洁能源持 续供电；Its application has boosted battery storage 把因果反过来说成 \"清洁能源应 用→推动电池储能\"。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文 vehicle manufacturers, who are placing big bets on battery-powered electric vehicles 是 \"车企押注电动车（即用电池/清洁能源驱动汽车）\"，主体是汽车制造业用清 洁能源；而 It is commonly used in car manufacturing 表达 \"清洁能源被广泛用在汽 车制造（生产环节）\"，把驱动汽车偷换为生产汽车。且 commonly used 与原文 still a rarity 也方向相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"keep power flowing around the clock more likely ↔ Its continuous supply is becoming a reality this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years ↔ Its continuous supply is becoming a reality 预判 \"不间断供电正变成现实\" 与 Its continuous supply is becoming a reality 在主体 （清洁能源）、状态（不间断/持续）、趋势（正成为现实）三方面完全对位。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文 more likely 与 could change the picture rapidly 都呈现 \"前景看好、走向可行\" 的态度；Its sustainable exploitation will remain difficult 表达 \"可持续利用将依然困 难\"，与原文方向完全相反。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：Which of the following is true about clean energy according to Paragraphs 5&6? 是 问 \"以下哪项为真\"，要求选与原文事实一致的选项。","拆句：Which of the following is true about clean energy according to Paragraphs 5&6? 是 疑问句，Which 是主语，is 系动词，true 是表语，about clean energy 和 according to Paragraphs 5&6 是两个介词短语作状语兼范围限定；结构清晰、无陷阱。","定位：The question \"what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?\" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely. \"风停日落时怎么办？\" 这个问题一直是质疑者快速否定可再生能源的口实；但电池储能能力 的提升正在让可再生能源昼夜不间断供电的能力更趋可行。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第47—60页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: The question "what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely. "
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第1—970页；原文定位：The question "what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely. "风停日落时怎么办？" 这个问题一直是质疑者快速否定可再生能源的口实；但电池储能能力 的提升正在让可再生能源昼夜不间断供电的能力更趋可行。

questions.content: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that renewable energy____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "will bring the US closer to other countries", "B": "will accelerate global environmental change", "C": "is not really encouraged by the US government", "D": "is not competitive enough with regard to its cost"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文 at a time of a global shift in thought 只是指出全球思维在变，并未说美国将与 其他国家关系靠近；will bring the US closer to other countries 中 \"使美国与他国走 近\" 系凭空推断。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文 to have a meaningful effect in slowing climate change 表明可再生能源是在 \"减缓\"（slow） 气候变化；will accelerate global environmental change 表达 \"加速 全球环境变化\"，与 slow 方向相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"What Washington does – or doesn't do – to promote alternative energy ↔ is not really encouraged by the US government President Trump has underlined fossil fuels – especially coal – as the path to economic growth. In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source. ↔ is not really encouraged by the US government 预判 \"美国政府其实没真推动可再生能源\" 与 is not really encouraged by the US government 在主体、立场两方面完全对位；not really 这一含蓄否定贴合作者尾段的 反讽语气。"},"D":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"原文尾段未谈及成本，is not competitive enough with regard to its cost 提到的 \"成 本竞争力不足\" 完全没有出现在尾段；成本话题在第 2 段反而以 \"价格暴跌、太阳能板降 价 80%\" 正向表达过，方向反转。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：It can be inferred from the last paragraph that renewable energy____. 含 inferred，要 求由原文一步推出结论。","拆句：It can be inferred from the last paragraph that renewable energy____. 是形式主语 it + 被动语态 can be inferred + that 宾语从句的复合句；从句主语 renewable energy 后谓语 由选项补全；注意从句中的内容才是要推断的对象，不要把 the last paragraph 当作推断 对象。","定位：What Washington does – or doesn't do – to promote alternative energy may mean less and less at a time of a global shift in thought. 在全球思想转变的当下，华盛顿（美国政府）做什么或不做什么来推动替代能源，可能越来 越无关紧要。"]

questions.content: Linking phone numbers to Facebook identities may____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "worsen political disputes", "B": "mess up customer records", "C": "pose a risk to Facebook users", "D": "mislead the European commission"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"过度推断：把举例上升为结论","explanation":"原文用 Theresa May 政争只是举例说明关联手机号会带来怎样的暴露，作者并未声称这 种关联本身会 \"加剧政治争端\"，worsen political disputes 是把例子拔高成结论。"},"B":{"trapType":"张冠李戴：用别处的对象冒充本题对象","explanation":"the records of which customers have purchased what 是同段后半句对 Whole Foods 的另一处讨论，根本不是 Facebook 关联手机号的后果，mess up customer records 把对象张冠李戴。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be ↔ pose a risk to Facebook users Theresa May's enemies are currently plotting ↔ pose a risk to Facebook users 预判落在 \"对用户的风险\"，四个选项中只有 pose a risk to Facebook users 把后果落 在用户身上，其他三项分别滑向政治、客户记录、欧盟。"},"D":{"trapType":"答非所问：用前提冒充后果","explanation":"原文 Facebook promised the European commission then that it would not link... but it broke the promise 描述的是 Facebook 已经食言这一事实，作者并未把 may____ 的后果落在 \"误导欧委会\" 上，mislead the European commission 与题干指 向不符。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：Linking phone numbers to Facebook identities may____ 用 may 引出可能的后果，要求 考生在原文事实基础上做一步语义延伸。","拆句：题干主干为 \"Linking phone numbers to Facebook identities may +动词原形\"，动名词 短语作主语，选项是 may 后的谓语动词部分，结构清晰、无陷阱。","定位：Even without knowing what was in the messages, the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be. questions.content: According to the author, competition law____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "should serve the new market powers", "B": "may worsen the economic imbalance", "C": "should not provide just one legal solution", "D": "cannot keep pace with the changing market"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"与原文相反：把作者立场反转","explanation":"作者全段在指出 competition law 缺陷、并提出 \"按现行解释存在问题\"，立场是批评， 根本没有 \"该为新市场势力服务\" 之意，should serve the new market powers 与作者 立场相反。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有：嫁接未提及的负面后果","explanation":"原文说 competition law 是 the only way to address these imbalances of power， 作者认为它有缺陷但并未说它会 \"加剧经济失衡\"，may worsen the economic imbalance 属无中生有。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反：把 only 反转为 not just one","explanation":"原文恰恰说 competition law the only way，作者并未主张 \"不该只提供一种法律方 案\"，should not provide just one legal solution 与原文相反或无中生有。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy ↔ cannot keep pace with the changing market By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace ↔ cannot keep pace with the changing market 预判是 \"跟不上数字经济变化的节奏\"，四个选项里只有 cannot keep pace with the changing market 与之直接对应，其余三项要么扭曲立场、要么主张未提。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：According to the author, competition law____ 要求复述作者对 competition law 的具体 评价，属于事实复述层面。","拆句：题干为不完整陈述句 \"competition law____\"，选项是谓语部分；\"According to the author\" 是状语，只是限定信息来源，不影响主干判断。","定位：For one thing, it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy. questions.content: Competition law as presently interpreted can hardly protect Facebook users because____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "they are not defined as customers", "B": "they are not financially reliable", "C": "the services are generally digital", "D": "the services are paid for by advertisers"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"The users of their services are not their customers ↔ they are not defined as customers Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them ↔ they are not defined as customers 预判落在 \"用户不算客户\" 的法律身份问题上，they are not defined as customers 是 唯一直接对应该原因的选项。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念：把 financial 的方向反转","explanation":"原文 financial disadvantage to consumers 说的是 \"用户的经济损失不明显\"，并不是 说 \"用户在财务上不可靠\"；they are not financially reliable 把 \"无经济损失\" 偷换为 \"不可信赖\"。"},"C":{"trapType":"答非所问：拿话题标签代替真正原因","explanation":"原文从未声称 \"数字服务\" 本身导致竞争法无法保护用户，真正障碍是用户身份不是客 户；the services are generally digital 属答非所问。"},"D":{"trapType":"答非所问：把附带信息当主因","explanation":"原文确实说 That would be the people who buy advertising from them，但只是顺 带交代 \"真正的客户是广告主\"，并不是用 \"广告主付费\" 来解释 \"用户为何得不到保 护\"，选项把附加信息当作 because 的核心，属答非所问。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：can hardly protect Facebook users because____ 中的 because 直接索要原文已写出的原 因，是典型细节题。","拆句：主干为 \"Competition law... can hardly protect Facebook users because+从句\"；can hardly 是含蓄否定，等同于 cannot really protect，考生务必读出 \"几乎无法保护\" 的否定 意味。","定位：Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them. The users of their services are not their customers. 按现行解释，竞争法处理的是消费者的经济损失，而当这些服务的用户不付费时，这种损失 并不明显。这些服务的用户并不是它们的客户。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第61—74页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them. The users of their services are not their customers.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第1—788页；原文定位：Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them. The users of their services are not their customers. 按现行解释，竞争法处理的是消费者的经济损失，而当这些服务的用户不付费时，这种损失 并不明显。这些服务的用户并不是它们的客户。

questions.content: The ants analogy is used to illustrate____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "a win-win business model between digital giants", "B": "a typical competition pattern among digital giants", "C": "the benefits provided for digital giants' customers", "D": "the relationship between digital giants and their users"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正话反说 + 范围偷换","explanation":"原文确实说 even if both sides benefit，但作者用 \"It doesn't feel like a human or democratic relationship\" 表态：这不是健康的关系，更不是 win-win business model；a win-win business model between digital giants 把作者明确否定的乐观面 当作类比目的，且把范围限制在 \"巨头之间\"，对象也错。"},"B":{"trapType":"张冠李戴：换比喻对象","explanation":"原文类比的是 Google 与用户的关系，根本没有讨论 \"巨头之间\" 的竞争；a typical competition pattern among digital giants 把对象张冠李戴，并捏造 competition 这 个不存在的话题。"},"C":{"trapType":"以偏概全 + 偷换概念","explanation":"原文 Gmail keeps the spammers out of our inboxes 只是说蚂蚁与 Google 都给被养 的一方挡掉天敌，是类比的延伸而非主旨；作者总体立场是用户为巨头服务、巨头从用 户身上获利，选项 the benefits provided for digital giants' customers 把次要让步当 主旨，且 customers 一词与第 3 段 \"用户不是客户\" 直接矛盾。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield ↔ the relationship between digital giants and their users Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed ↔ the relationship between digital giants and their users 预判落在 \"巨头与用户的关系\"，四个选项中只有 the relationship between digital giants and their users 直接覆盖类比映射的两方关系。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：The ants analogy is used to illustrate____ 直接问类比的论证目的，是典型例证目的题。","拆句：主干 \"The ants analogy is used to illustrate____\"，is used to do 是固定句型 \"被用来做 某事\"，空格填名词性成分（论点），结构清晰、无陷阱。","定位：The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants. Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield. 他们卖的产品是数据，而我们这些用户把自己的生活转化为数据，为数字巨头服务。正如有 些蚂蚁饲养名为蚜虫的小虫，以获取它们进食时产生的蜜露一样，Google 也在饲养我们， 以获取我们数字生活产出的数据。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第61—74页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants. Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第1—975页；原文定位：The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants. Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield. 他们卖的产品是数据，而我们这些用户把自己的生活转化为数据，为数字巨头服务。正如有 些蚂蚁饲养名为蚜虫的小虫，以获取它们进食时产生的蜜露一样，Google 也在饲养我们， 以获取我们数字生活产出的数据。

questions.content: The key to mastering the art of deep work is to____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "keep to your focus time", "B": "list your immediate tasks", "C": "make specific daily plans", "D": "seize every minute to work"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"determine your length of focus time and stick to it ↔ keep to your focus time 预判要求「确定专注时长并坚持」,A 选项 keep to your focus time 把「坚持」与「专 注时间」两个语义点都对上,与定位句等值,故选 A。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"list your immediate tasks 在原文 P1 P2 里没有任何对应——文章没有让你「列出眼前 的任务」,而是要你「圈出专注时间」。这是把考研二考生熟悉的「任务清单」概念塞进 来制造熟悉感。"},"C":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"make specific daily plans 对应的是 plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day 那项研究里被打击积极性的做法,而且 the detailed daily plans demotivated students 已说明这种做法是负面的,绝不是 deep work 的关键。题干问的 是 deep work 的关键,C 把别处的概念错位安到这里。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"seize every minute to work 把「每分钟都用来工作」塞给读者,但 the key is to determine your length of focus time 强调的是「圈出一段时长」而不是「分分秒秒地 工作」;而且后文 embrace downtime 与 Idleness ... is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done 还专门反对「分秒必争」。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：The key to mastering the art of deep work is to 不含 infer / suggest / imply 等推断词, 而是问一个明确事实——掌握 deep work 的关键是什么,定位到原文相应句子即可得答案。","拆句：题干主干 The key to mastering the art of deep work is to 是 The key (主语) + is to (系 动词 + 不定式表语) 的结构,选项是 to 后面的动词短语,补全后构成完整句子。结构平铺直叙, 无陷阱。","定位：Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it. 无论采用哪种方法,关键都是确定你专注时间的长度,并坚持下去。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第75—89页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第1—741页；原文定位：Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it. 无论采用哪种方法,关键都是确定你专注时间的长度,并坚持下去。

questions.content: The study in the early 1980s cited by Harford shows that____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "distractions may actually increase efficiency", "B": "daily schedules are indispensable to studying", "C": "students are hardly motivated by monthly goals", "D": "detailed plans may not be as fruitful as expected"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"distractions may actually increase efficiency 的 increase efficiency 在原文里没有依 据。leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results 只说 「留余地能取得最好效果」,并未说「干扰能提高效率」;题干问的是研究 shows 什么,而 非 Harford 之后引申的主张。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"daily schedules are indispensable to studying 的 indispensable 与原文完全相反 ——原文 the detailed daily plans demotivated students 恰恰否定了详细日计划的必 要性。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"students are hardly motivated by monthly goals 谈的是月度目标对学生的激励效果, 但原文 set out monthly goals and study activities 只交代了对照组的设置,从未给出 「月度目标几乎不能激励学生」的结论。原文要否定的是详细日计划,不是月度目标。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students ↔ detailed plans may not be as fruitful as expected detailed daily plans ↔ detailed plans 预判要求「详尽日计划没有预期那么好」,D 用 may not be as fruitful as expected 严 格对应了「研究者以为最有效→实际错了」的反转,故选 D。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：The study in the early 1980s cited by Harford shows that 用 shows 引出研究结果,问的 是该研究的客观结论,属可直接定位的细节题。","拆句：题干 The study in the early 1980s cited by Harford shows that 主干为 The study shows that...,cited by Harford 是过去分词短语后置修饰 study,in the early 1980s 是时间 状语修饰 study。三层修饰都附在主语上,选项接在 that 之后充当宾语从句。结构清晰、无 陷阱。","定位：While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students. 尽管研究者们原以为结构良好的日计划在执行任务时最有效,但他们错了:详尽的日计划反倒 让学生失去了动力。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第75—89页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第1—796页；原文定位：While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students. 尽管研究者们原以为结构良好的日计划在执行任务时最有效,但他们错了:详尽的日计划反倒 让学生失去了动力。

questions.content: According to Newport, idleness is____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "a desirable mental state for busy people", "B": "a major contributor to physical health", "C": "an effective way to save time and energy", "D": "an essential factor in accomplishing any work"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"a desirable mental state for busy people 把 idleness 偷换成 a mental state,并加上 for busy people 的对象限定,但原文 Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice 明确否定了「闲适即某种状态」的简单表述,且对象是所有人脑,不是「忙人」 专属。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"a major contributor to physical health 把 idleness 的作用对象偷换成 physical health 身体健康;原文 as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body 只 是用 vitamin D 对 body 的关系作类比,被类比的本体是 idleness 对 brain,不是 idleness 对 body。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"an effective way to save time and energy 中的 save time and energy 在 P7 全段没 有任何对应——Newport 谈的是 idleness 与 getting any work done 的关系,而非 「省时省力」。这是把整篇文章 make the most of our focus and energy 等措辞拼凑 过来的伪贴合。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"necessary to getting any work done ↔ an essential factor in accomplishing any work 预判要求「完成任何工作离不开闲适」,D 用 an essential factor in accomplishing any work 严格对应 necessary to getting any work done,故选 D。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：According to Newport, idleness is 是 According to + 人名 的标准句式,问该人物对 idleness 的明确表述,属细节题。","拆句：题干 According to Newport, idleness is 结构是 According to Newport (状语) + idleness (主语) + is (系动词),选项是补全表语。语序简单,无陷阱。","定位：Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body…[idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done. 闲适并不仅仅是度假、放纵或恶习;它对大脑就如同维生素 D 对身体一样不可或缺……反讽的 是,正是闲适才使得任何工作得以完成。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第75—89页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body…[idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第1—842页；原文定位：Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body…[idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done. 闲适并不仅仅是度假、放纵或恶习;它对大脑就如同维生素 D 对身体一样不可或缺……反讽的 是,正是闲适才使得任何工作得以完成。

questions.content: Pillay believes that our brains' shift between being focused and unfocused____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "can result in psychological well-being", "B": "can bring about greater efficiency", "C": "is aimed at better balance in work", "D": "is driven by task urgency"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"can result in psychological well-being 中 psychological well-being 心理健康在 P8 与 P9 没有任何对应——Pillay 谈的是 productivity 和 efficiency,而不是「心理 福祉」。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"they tend to be more efficient ↔ can bring about greater efficiency 预判要求「切换专注与放空更高效」,B 用 can bring about greater efficiency 严格复 刻这一语义,故选 B。"},"C":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"is aimed at better balance in work 中 aimed at 强加目的性——原文只说大脑切换时 「更高效」,并未说这种切换「是为了取得工作平衡」。is aimed at 暗含「有意识地为了 某目的」,是把客观机制偷偷拔高成主观意图。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"is driven by task urgency 中 task urgency 任务紧迫性在原文从未出现——Pillay 谈的 是大脑机制本身,不是任务紧不紧急。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：Pillay believes that our brains' shift between being focused and unfocused 问 Pillay 相信此种切换会带来什么,要求回原文找他被引用的观点句,属细节题。","拆句：题干 Pillay believes that our brains' shift between being focused and unfocused 主干 是 Pillay believes that...,that 引出宾语从句,主语是 our brains' shift,shift 后接 between A and B 介词短语作后置修饰,选项是宾语从句的谓语部分。注意 our brains' shift 是名词性 所有格,shift 是名词不是动词。","定位：When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient. 当我们的大脑在专注于某项任务与放空之间来回切换时,它们往往更高效。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第75—89页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2018年真题及答案解析（整卷） (1).pdf，PDF第1—524页；原文定位：When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient. 当我们的大脑在专注于某项任务与放空之间来回切换时,它们往往更高效。

questions.content: This text is mainly about____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "ways to relieve the tension of busy life", "B": "approaches to getting more done in less time", "C": "the key to eliminating distractions", "D": "the cause of the lack of focus time"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"ways to relieve the tension of busy life 中 relieve the tension「缓解忙碌生活的紧张 感」只是 P6 embrace downtime 和 P7 Idleness 这一两段的局部主题,并不能涵盖 P1 至 P5 关于 deep work、deep scheduling、to-do list 的内容,也不涵盖 P8 至 P9 的脑 科学解释。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"Another approach to getting more done in less time ↔ approaches to getting more done in less time get more done in less time ↔ getting more done in less time 预判要求「如何用更少时间完成更多事」,B 用 approaches to getting more done in less time 几乎字面对应原文 Another approach to getting more done in less time, 且覆盖 P1 至 P9 各段招式,故选 B。"},"C":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"the key to eliminating distractions 中 eliminating distractions「消除干扰」只是 P3 combat constant interruptions 的局部话题,且原文从未主张「完全消除」(eliminate), 反而 leaving room for improvisation 主张为干扰留余地。既不覆盖全文,又与文章具体 主张相反。"},"D":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"the cause of the lack of focus time 的 the cause 是「原因」,但全文从未追溯「为什 么缺乏专注时间」的成因,而是给出多种「如何完成更多事」的解决方案。题干问 mainly about,选项却给「原因」,方向完全错。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：This text is mainly about 中 mainly about 是主旨题的标准触发词,直接判定为主旨题、走 特殊路径。","拆句：题干 This text is mainly about 是 主语 + 系动词 + 介词 about 的结构,选项是 about 后面 的宾语短语。结构最简,无陷阱。"]

questions.content: According to Paragraph 1, one motive in imposing the new rule is to____
questions.options_json: {"A": "enhance bankers' sense of responsibility.", "B": "help corporations achieve larger profits.", "C": "build a new system of financial regulation.", "D": "guarantee the bonuses of top executives."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking ↔ enhance bankers' sense of responsibility 预判「让银行家担责」与 enhance bankers' sense of responsibility 是同一语义的两 种说法，无须二次推理即可锁定。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文远期愿景是 to build a stronger economy for future generations——是「更强 的经济」，而非帮企业「赚更多利润」，把宏观经济目标偷换成微观利润目标。"},"C":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"原文说监管者 have imposed a rather unusual rule——只是在既有体系上加一条规 则，并未「构建一套新的金融监管体系」。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文是 any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years——奖 金被「延迟」发放，是约束高管的手段，目的恰恰是让他们忌惮，而不是去「保障」他 们的奖金。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：According to Paragraph 1, one motive in imposing the new rule is to____ 把范围直接 锁在一段之内，问一个具体动机——典型的段内细节题。","拆句：句子主干是 one motive ... is to____，主系表结构，待补全部分是 to 不定式，做表语。介 词短语 in imposing the new rule 修饰 motive，说明动机针对的是哪件事。结构平铺直 叙，无陷阱。","定位：The main purpose of this \"clawback\" rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk- taking and to restore public trust in financial institutions. 这条「追回」规则的主要目的，是让银行家为有害的冒险行为承担责任，并恢复公众对金融 机构的信任。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语一2019年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第42—56页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: The main purpose of this "clawback" rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk- taking and to restore public trust in financial institutions.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语一2019年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第1—496页；原文定位：The main purpose of this "clawback" rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk- taking and to restore public trust in financial institutions. 这条「追回」规则的主要目的，是让银行家为有害的冒险行为承担责任，并恢复公众对金融 机构的信任。

questions.content: Alfred Marshall is quoted to indicate____
questions.options_json: {"A": "the conditions for generating quick profits.", "B": "governments' impatience in decision-making.", "C": "the solid structure of publicly traded companies.", "D": "\"short-termism\" in economic activities."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文是用比喻批评追逐 quick profits 的心态，根本没在谈「产生快钱需要什么条件」， 选项把负面被批的对象偷换成正面的方法论。"},"B":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"原文聚焦 publicly traded companies 的短期主义，从未提及 governments；把主语 从公司张冠到政府，无中生有。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文是 has worsened in publicly traded companies——上市公司里短期主义正在恶 化，根本不是说其结构 solid。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"\"Short-termism\" or the desire for quick profits, has worsened in publicly traded companies ↔ \"short-termism\" in economic activities Haldane 借 Marshall 的 children 比喻，是要让读者直观感受 short-termism 的本质 （贪图眼前、不愿等待），所以答案必然回到 short-termism 自身——精准对应 D。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：Alfred Marshall is quoted to indicate____ 直问「引用为了表明什么」——典型的例证/引 证目的题。","拆句：被动句：Alfred Marshall is quoted to indicate____，主语是被引者本人，is quoted 是 被动谓语，to indicate 是不定式做目的状语，问的是「谁引他、为了表明什么」。结构无 陷阱。","定位：\"Short-termism\" or the desire for quick profits, has worsened in publicly traded companies, says the Bank of England's top economist, Andrew Haldane. questions.content: The author examines the practice of grade forgiveness by____
questions.options_json: {"A": "assessing its feasibility.", "B": "analyzing the causes behind it.", "C": "comparing different views on it.", "D": "listing its long-run effects."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"feasibility（可行性）需要讨论“能不能做、有什么条件、可否推广”；全文谈的是“为什么 会有这种做法”而非“能否实施”——grade forgiveness 早已在执行，根本不存在可行性 讨论。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"For public institutions, state funds are sometimes tied partly to their success on metrics such as graduation rates and student retention – so better grades can, by boosting figures like those, mean more money ↔ analyzing the causes behind it grade forgiveness is just another way that universities are responding to consumers' expectations for higher education ↔ analyzing the causes behind it 预判“层层挖掘背后原因”与 analyzing the causes behind it 完全对位，is 用 analyzing 这一元动词概括了 P1→P5→P6 一脉相承的归因动作。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"compare different views 要求文中至少存在两个明确对立的观点被并列对照评估；P4 的“官方说法”与 P5 的“学校真实利益”虽有 That said 的轻转折，但作者并未把它们并列 权衡，而是用前者作铺垫去引出后者——这是“挖原因”的递进，不是“并列对比观点”。"},"D":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"long-run effects 要求作者列出该做法对教育/就业/社会等的长期后果；全文除了 P6 末 句一笔带过“产出合格毕业生”外，根本未展开任何长期影响，只是反复在拆原因。"}}

questions.options_json: {"A": "can remember other rats' facial features.", "B": "differentiate smells better than sizes.", "C": "respond more to actions than to looks.", "D": "can be scared by a plastic box on wheels."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"can remember other rats' facial features 把 facial features 拼到 other rats 身上， 但原文 facial features 是说机器鼠是否需要装面部特征，并非老鼠记忆同伴的面部。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"differentiate smells better than sizes 说老鼠辨别气味比辨别体型强，但原文 put a scent on it 只在讨论是否要给机器鼠喷气味，没有任何 \"smells vs sizes\" 的比较。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"a moving head and tail, facial features, and put a scent on it ↔ looks but that wasn't necessary ↔ respond more to actions than to looks followed the living rats around, played with the same toys, and opened cage doors ↔ actions C 项把 but that wasn't necessary 中\"外观不必要\"和前文 social 机器鼠靠行为赢得老 鼠认同的事实合并起来，得出\"老鼠更看重行为而非外观\"的结论。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"can be scared by a plastic box on wheels 说老鼠被装轮子的塑料盒吓到，但原文 The readiness of the rats to befriend the social robot was surprising given its minimal design 强调的是\"老鼠竟然愿意与之交朋友\"，方向相反。"}}

questions.content: Which is considered a weakness of the city-level measures to tackle dirty air?
questions.options_json: {"A": "They are biased against car manufacturers.", "B": "They prove impractical for city councils.", "C": "They are deemed too mild for politicians.", "D": "They put too much burden on individual motorists."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"They are biased against car manufacturers 说措施 \"对汽车制造商不公平\"，但原文 rather than on to the car manufacturers whose cheating is the real cause of our toxic pollution 恰恰是在指责制造商造假却没承担成本——\"反向偏袒\" 司机才是问题， 不是 \"反向偏袒\" 制造商。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"They prove impractical for city councils 说措施 \"对市议会来说不切实际\"，原文从未 讨论市议会执行是否可行的问题；作者只说措施 politically controversial, and therefore vulnerable——政治上有争议、因此脆弱，与 \"实操不可行\" 不是同一回事。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"They are deemed too mild for politicians 称措施 \"被认为对政客而言太温和\"，原文 politically controversial 说的是 \"在政治上有争议\"——意指有人反对、易被推翻，并未 说 \"措施温和\"。\"政治上的争议性\" 与 \"对政客而言温和\" 不是一回事。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"put the costs of cleaning the air on to individual drivers ↔ put too much burden on individual motorists 预判的 \"负担落到普通司机/车主身上\" 与 put too much burden on individual motorists 在主谓宾三个成分上完全等值；这正是 rather than on to the car manufacturers 反向对比所凸显的 weakness 内容。选 D。"}}

questions.content: What might have kept the Victorians from smiling for pictures in the 1890s?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Their inherent social sensitiveness.", "B": "Their tension before the camera.", "C": "Their distrust of new inventions.", "D": "Their unhealthy dental condition."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"Their inherent social sensitiveness 把原因拔高到 \"维多利亚人天生敏感的社会 性\"——原文只说 the loss of dignity 这一具体顾虑，没有把它归因于民族性格特征。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文未提维多利亚人在相机前 tension 紧张；只说他们怕失体面、不愿露齿，与 \"紧张\" 是两个心理范畴。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"distrust of new inventions \"不信任新发明\" 在原文毫无依据——文章只把曝光时间问 题归到 P3P4 早期技术限制，并未说维多利亚人不信任相机这种新发明。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene ↔ Their unhealthy dental condition before the birth of proper dentistry ↔ Their unhealthy dental condition 定位句给出明确因果：因为牙齿状况差，露齿笑会失体面，所以维多利亚人不笑——这 正是 D 项 Their unhealthy dental condition 的内核。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 What might have kept the Victorians from smiling for pictures in the 1890s? 虽 用 might，但问的是文中已给出的解释，原文会直接交代原因。","拆句：What might have kept the Victorians from smiling for pictures in the 1890s? 中 might have kept 是 \"might + have done\" 的虚拟/推测完成时，表示对过去的推测； keep sb from doing 是固定搭配，意为 \"阻止某人做某事\"。注意 from smiling 不是否定 smile，整句是问 \"什么阻止了他们笑\"。","定位：One explanation might be the loss of dignity displayed through a cheesy grin. \"Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth,\" ran one popular Victorian maxim, alluding to the fact that before the birth of proper dentistry, mouths were often in a shocking state of hygiene. 一种解释可能是：露齿傻笑会失体面。当时流行的一句格言说 \"造物给我们嘴唇是为遮住牙 齿\"，暗指在正规牙科诞生之前，人们的口腔卫生状况骇人。"]

questions.content: Mark Twain is quoted to show that the disapproval of smiles in pictures was____
questions.options_json: {"A": "a deep-root belief.", "B": "a misguided attitude.", "C": "a controversial view.", "D": "a thought-provoking idea."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that ... \"nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever\" ↔ a deep-root belief it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons ↔ a deep-root belief Even 让步 + Mark Twain 这一爱笑的反例都接受 \"傻笑可耻\" 的观点，说明这种 disapproval 不是某人的偏见而是全社会共享的根深观念，正是 a deep-root belief。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"a misguided attitude 是说这种态度 \"被误导、不正确\"，但作者只在客观陈述维多利亚 人的看法，没有贬抑它；说 Mark Twain 等人的态度 \"被误导\" 与原文的中立陈述方向 相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"a controversial view \"有争议的观点\" 暗示存在正反两方分歧；原文一面倒地呈现 \"反对 露齿微笑\"，没有提及任何持反方观点的声音，谈不上 controversial。"},"D":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"a thought-provoking idea \"发人深省的想法\" 是把作者的中立举证当作他在赞许马克· 吐温的话；原文没有任何句子表达 \"这值得深思\" 的色彩，只是为论证 \"厌笑\" 的普遍性 服务。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 Mark Twain is quoted to show that the disapproval of smiles in pictures was____ 用 \"is quoted to show that\" 明确问 \"引用此人是为了说明什么\"，是典型的例证目的题。","拆句：Mark Twain is quoted to show that the disapproval of smiles in pictures was____ 中 is quoted 是被动语态，\"被引用\"；to show that ... 是不定式作目的状语，that 引导宾语从 句；从句主语是 the disapproval of smiles in pictures，谓语 was 后空缺由选项补足。理 解关键是把 to show 看作 \"目的\"，问的是 \"引用他的目的是说明 disapproval 是怎样的一 种东西\"。","定位：A toothy grin (especially when there were gaps or blackened gnashers) lacked class: drunks, tramps, and music hall performers might gurn and grin with a smile as wide as Lewis Carroll's gum-exposing Cheshire Cat, but it was not a becoming look for properly bred persons. Even Mark Twain, a man who enjoyed a hearty laugh, said that when it came to photographic portraits there could be \"nothing more damning than a silly, foolish smile fixed forever\". 露齿笑（尤其有牙缝或黑牙时）很掉档次：醉汉、流浪汉、音乐厅艺人也许会咧嘴大笑，笑 得像刘易斯·卡罗尔笔下露牙龈的柴郡猫一样宽，但这对于教养良好之人并非得体之相。甚至 连爱开怀大笑的马克·吐温也说，谈到肖像照，\"再没有什么比一个永远定格的傻里傻气的笑 容更糟的了\"。"]

questions.content: There has long been concern that broadband providers would____
questions.options_json: {"A": "bring web-based firms under control.", "B": "slow down the traffic on their network.", "C": "show partiality in treating clients.", "D": "intensify competition with their rivals."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"bring web-based firms under control 的意思是\"使互联网公司受其控制\"，但原文 advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried 说的是\"互联网公 司\"和\"消费者\"是 worried 的一方，不是被控制的一方；偏袒 ≠ 控制。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"slow down the traffic on their network 描述\"限速\"行为，原文首段并未提及，而是 favor affiliated websites over their rivals'——担忧的是\"偏袒\"而非\"限速\"。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"favor affiliated websites over their rivals' ↔ show partiality in treating clients 预判说的\"偏袒自家、冷落对手\"就是 show partiality in treating clients 的口语化版 本，二者语义同心。"},"D":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"intensify competition with their rivals 说的是宽带商与其\"对手\"竞争加剧，但原文 over their rivals' 中的 rivals 是被偏袒网站的对手（即\"网站\"的对手），不是宽带商自己 的对手；且原文是\"差别对待\"而非\"加剧竞争\"。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：There has long been concern that broadband providers would____ 是一个待补全的客 观叙述，问的是\"担忧的具体内容是什么\"——指向原文某句客观信息，不带 infer/imply。","拆句：There has long been concern that broadband providers would____ 是 \"There be + 名 词 + that 同位语从句\" 结构：concern 是抽象名词，that 后面是它的内容；空格补的是 broadband providers would ____ 这个从句的谓语动词原形。结构平铺，无陷阱。","定位：From the early days of broadband, advocates for consumers and web-based companies worried that the cable and phone companies selling broadband connections had the power and incentive to favor affiliated websites over their rivals'. 从宽带发展早期起，消费者权益倡导者和互联网公司就担心：销售宽带连接的有线电视和电 话公司，有权力也有动机偏袒与自己关联的网站，而冷落对手的网站。"]

questions.content: Judge Patricia Millett argues that the appeals court's decision____
questions.options_json: {"A": "focus on trivialities.", "B": "conveys an ambiguous message.", "C": "is at odds with its earlier rulings.", "D": "is out of touch with reality."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"focus on trivialities 说判决只盯小事；但 Millett 的批评是\"脱离现实\"而非\"专注琐 事\"——severity 和 focus 维度都不同。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"conveys an ambiguous message 说判决传递的信息模糊；但 Millett 的评价 unhinged from the realities 是明确的\"脱离现实\"判定，并非说判决本身意思含糊。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"is at odds with its earlier rulings 说判决与法院早先裁定相互矛盾；但 the appeals court unanimously upheld the 2017 order ... citing a Supreme Court ruling from 2005 that upheld a similarly deregulatory move 反而说本次判决与 2005 年的裁定 方向一致（都是去监管），不是矛盾；Millett 也没批评判决与早先裁定不符。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service ↔ is out of touch with reality 预判说\"脱节\"，out of touch with reality 就是这层意思的标准英语表达——锁定 D。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：Judge Patricia Millett argues that the appeals court's decision____ 要复述 Millett 的明 确观点，原文有逐字引语，属客观信息抽取，非主观推断。","拆句：Judge Patricia Millett argues that the appeals court's decision____：主句主语 Judge Patricia Millett，谓语 argues，其后是 that 宾语从句；空格补的是从句的谓语，即\"上诉法 院的决定怎么样\"。结构无陷阱，但要警惕\"是谁说的\"——这是 Millett 的话，不是法院本身 的话。","定位：But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that \"the result is unhinged from the realities of modern broadband service,\" and said Congress or the Supreme Court could intervene to \"avoid trapping Internet regulation in technological anachronism.\" 但 Millett 法官在协同意见中说得对：\"这一结果脱离了现代宽带服务的现实\"，并表示国会 或最高法院可以介入，\"以免把互联网监管困在技术时代错置之中\"。"]

questions.content: Some people argue that food self-sufficiency in the UK would____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "be hindered by its population growth", "B": "contribute to the nation's well-being", "C": "become a priority of the government", "D": "pose a challenge to its farming industry"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有：把背景信息当成论点内容","explanation":"be hindered by its population growth 在原文中无对应：首段虽提 With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050，但那是粮食安全的全球背 景，并非「某些人主张自给自足会如何」的内容。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"even the nation's health ↔ contribute to the nation's well-being 预判中三项支持理由之一是「国民健康」，选项 contribute to the nation's well-being 用 well-being 包住 health 这一具体维度，与定位句中 even the nation's health 完全 对应。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有：替政府表态","explanation":"become a priority of the government 在原文中无任何对应：定位句只列出三项支持 理由，并未提及政府的政策排序或优先级。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反：动词极性反转","explanation":"pose a challenge to its farming industry 与定位句 would boost the farming industry 极性相反：原文是「提振」农业，选项却说「对农业构成挑战」。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 Some people argue that food self-sufficiency in the UK would____ 是补全「某些 人主张自给自足会如何」的具体内容，要求复现原文中他人陈述的事实主张，无 infer / imply / suggest 等推断信号。","拆句：Some people argue that food self-sufficiency in the UK would____ 是「主句 + that 宾 语从句」结构，宾语从句缺谓语补足，选项即谓语短语；句子无否定无比较，理解上无陷 阱，关键是看清宾语从句的主语是 food self-sufficiency in the UK——回答的是「自给自 足这件事会带来什么」而非「英国会如何」。","定位：A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health. 支持者主张，重回自给自足将提振农业、政治主权、甚至国民健康。"]

questions.content: The report by the University of Leeds shows that in the UK____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "farmland has been inefficiently utilized", "B": "factory-style production needs reforming", "C": "most land is used for meat and dairy production", "D": "more green fields will be converted for farming"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"过度推断：把事实数字升级成价值评价","explanation":"farmland has been inefficiently utilized 在原文无对应：报告只陈述土地分配比例， 未做「低效」评价；80% 与 85% 的对比也只是产能事实，不等于「低效」。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念：把「需要更多 X」偷换成「X 需要改革」","explanation":"factory-style production needs reforming 偷换了第4段的 more factory-style production——原文是说要更自给自足就需要更多工厂化生产，并非说工厂化生产需要 改革。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production ↔ most land is used for meat and dairy production 预判中的「绝大多数国土用于肉与奶制品生产」与 most land is used for meat and dairy production 完全等价，是定位句的标准同义改写。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反：极性反转","explanation":"more green fields will be converted for farming 与第4段 fewer green fields and more factory-style production 方向相反——原文是绿地会更少、工厂化更多，不是 绿地变多去搞种植。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 The report by the University of Leeds shows that in the UK____，「shows that」 直接指向报告陈述的客观事实，属于细节定位与复述。","拆句：The report by the University of Leeds shows that in the UK____ 主干为 The report shows that…；by the University of Leeds 是后置定语修饰 report，in the UK 是 that 从 句中的地点状语；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。","定位：According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production. 据利兹大学一份关于英国食品生产的报告，英国 85% 的国土面积与肉奶生产相关。"]

questions.content: Crop-growing in the UK is restricted due to____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "its farming technology", "B": "its dietary tradition", "C": "its natural conditions", "D": "its commercial interests"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有：常识性归因","explanation":"its farming technology 在原文中无任何对应：定位句限制因素是土壤气候自然条件， 没有提及技术水平或机械化程度。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念：把段内相关词当成因果原因","explanation":"its dietary tradition 在原文中无对应：第5段开头虽提 a mainly plant-based diet wouldn't help，但讨论的是饮食结构能否解决供给问题，并非以「饮食传统」作为种植 受限原因。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"doesn't have the right soil or climate ↔ its natural conditions 预判要点是「土壤+气候」两项自然要素，its natural conditions 用 natural conditions 这一上位概念把两者打包覆盖，最贴合定位句。"},"D":{"trapType":"偷换概念：抓住关键词 commercial 改写其语法功能","explanation":"its commercial interests 误读了 to grow crops on a commercial basis——原文 commercial 只是修饰「商业化规模种植」这一种植标准，并非把「商业利益」作为限 制原因。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 Crop-growing in the UK is restricted due to____ 用 due to 直接索求原因，属于在 原文中找对应原因状语的细节题。","拆句：Crop-growing in the UK is restricted due to____ 是简单的「主-系-表 + due to」结构， be restricted 为被动语态，due to 后接原因；理解上无陷阱，关键是识别 due to 引导的 是「原因」而非「目的」。","定位：There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn't have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis. 英国以畜牧业为主是有原因的：其大部分地形的土壤或气候不适合商业化种植作物。"]

questions.content: It can be learned from the last paragraph that British people____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "rely largely on imports for fresh produce", "B": "enjoy a steady rise in fruit consumption", "C": "are seeking effective ways to cut calorie intake", "D": "are trying to grow new varieties of grains"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown ↔ rely largely on imports for fresh produce 预判要点是「大部分新鲜农产品依赖进口」，rely largely on imports for fresh produce 用 largely 量化补集，rely on imports 是 home-grown 反义的标准对应；属 典型的推断题正答。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有：杜撰时间趋势","explanation":"enjoy a steady rise in fruit consumption 在原文无对应：第6段只给出 23% 的当前比 例，未涉及水果消费量随时间的变化趋势。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反：把「需要更多」反转成「努力削减」","explanation":"are seeking effective ways to cut calorie intake 与原文方向相反：原文末句 we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake 是为了「找种这些作物的地」以满足热量摄 入，不是「想方设法削减」热量。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有：捏造科研行动","explanation":"are trying to grow new varieties of grains 在原文无对应：末段提及 grains 仅是讨论 种植空间不够的问题，未涉及「新品种培育」。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：It can be learned from the last paragraph that British people____ 中 It can be learned 是经典推断题标志词，要求在段内事实之上做一步合理延伸。","拆句：It can be learned from the last paragraph that British people____ 中 It 是形式主语，真 正主语是 that 从句；from the last paragraph 限定信息来源；待补的是 British people 的 谓语，无否定无比较，结构平直。","定位：Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs. 目前英国消费的水果蔬菜仅有 23% 是本土所产，即便采取最极端的措施也只能满足 30% 的 新鲜农产品需求。"]

questions.content: The author's attitude to food self-sufficiency in the UK is____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "defensive", "B": "doubtful", "C": "tolerant", "D": "optimistic"}

questions.content: What is true about Wunderlist and Sunrise after their acquisitions?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Their engineers were retained.", "B": "Their market values declined.", "C": "Their tech features improved.", "D": "Their products were re-priced."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"Their teams of engineers stayed on ↔ Their engineers were retained 预判要找「工程师 + 留下」的语义，A 项 Their engineers were retained 主谓完全对 应，无多余信息，无信息缺失，是定位句的标准同义替换。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"Their market values declined 谈两款 app 被收购后的「市场价值下降」，但文章 P2 只说被砍掉、工程师留下，从未提两款 app 自身有过市场价值衡量，更未提下降。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"Their tech features improved 称两款 app 的技术特性得到提升，但 P2 明确 Both apps, however, were later scrapped，两款 app 整体被砍掉，何来「自身特性提 升」；原文只说 Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products ——好特性被用进微软自家产品，而非 app 自身变好。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"Their products were re-priced 称产品被重新定价，但原文从头至尾未涉及任何定价行 为——产品已被「scrapped（砍掉）」，根本谈不上重新定价。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：What is true about Wunderlist and Sunrise after their acquisitions 用 What is true 直 接问事实，没有 infer/imply/suggest 这类推断信号，属于典型细节题。","拆句：题干 What is true about Wunderlist and Sunrise after their acquisitions 主干 What is true，介词短语 about ... after ... 双重限定主语——「关于这两个 app」「在被收购之 后」，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。","定位：Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products. Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many \"acqui- hires\" that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent. 然而，在微软表示已把这两款 app 的最佳功能用在自家产品里之后，两款 app 都被砍掉 了。但它们的工程师团队留了下来，使其成为大公司众多「acqui-hires（为人才而收购）」 案例中的两例——大公司借此满足对科技人才的巨大渴求。"]

questions.content: Microsoft's critics believe that the big tech companies tend to____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "exaggerate their product quality", "B": "eliminate their potential competitors", "C": "treat new tech talent unfairly", "D": "ignore public opinions"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"exaggerate their product quality 称大公司夸大自身产品质量，但 critics 在 P3 没 有一句话涉及「产品质量」「夸大宣传」——他们指控的是收购扼杀行为，不是营销 宣传。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors ↔ eliminate their potential competitors 预判要找「消灭/扼杀 + 潜在竞争对手」的语义，B 项 eliminate their potential competitors 在动词和宾语两端都与原文等值，无多余、无遗漏。"},"C":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"treat new tech talent unfairly 称大公司不公平对待新科技人才，但 P2 明确 Their teams of engineers stayed on 并把这些工程师称作 \"acqui-hires\"——大公司是为了 得到人才才收购，工程师反而被留下，并无「不公平」之说；critics 在 P3 的指控也不 是关于人才待遇。"},"D":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"ignore public opinions 称大公司无视公众舆论，但 critics 在 P3 的指控完全不涉及 「公众舆论」或「公司对舆论的态度」；段末 Microsoft declined to comment 只是微 软不予置评的一句客观陈述，不能反推为「无视公众舆论」。"}}

questions.content: Paul Arnold is concerned that small acquisitions might____.

questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"It was headed alternately by artists and scientists 中的 headed alternately（轮流 领导）原文没有任何依据——原文只说创办者刻意聚焦于光，未谈领导层如何轮换。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration ↔ It exemplified valuable art-science alliances looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa ↔ valuable art-science alliances 预判要求选\"它是有价值的艺-科合作范例\"，It exemplified valuable art-science alliances 在 exemplify、valuable、art-science alliances 三个要素上严丝合缝。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"Its projects aimed at advancing visual studies 把 CAVS 项目的目的偷换为\"推进视觉 研究\"；原文明示项目是为了 explore the role of technology in culture，\"visual studies\" 只是因为聚焦于光而出现在名字里，并不是项目要推进的对象。"},"D":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"Its founders sought to raise the status of artists 中的 raise the status of artists （提高艺术家地位）原文没有依据——原文说创办者把项目聚焦在光上，未提及他们想 抬高艺术家身份。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 What does the author say about CAYS? 是对作者就该机构所说内容的客观转述，属 于典型细节题问法。","拆句：题干为疑问句，主干 What does the author say about CAYS?，What 作 say 的宾语， about CAYS 是状语指明话题；结构平铺、无陷阱。","定位：More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture. The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the \"visual studies\" in the name. Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration. 半个多世纪前，麻省理工学院创办了\"先进视觉研究中心\"（CAVS），以探索技术在文化中 的角色。创办者刻意把项目聚焦在\"光\"上——所以名字里有\"视觉研究\"。光是艺术家和科学 家都感兴趣的事物，因此能成为他们合作的基础。"]

Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration.

Light was something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration. 半个多世纪前，麻省理工学院创办了"先进视觉研究中心"（CAVS），以探索技术在文化中 的角色。创办者刻意把项目聚焦在"光"上——所以名字里有"视觉研究"。光是艺术家和科学 家都感兴趣的事物，因此能成为他们合作的基础。

questions.content: In the last paragraph, the author holds that art-science collaborations ____
questions.options_json: {"A": "are likely to go beyond public expectations.", "B": "will intensify interdisciplinary competition.", "C": "should do more than communicating science.", "D": "are becoming more popular than before."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"are likely to go beyond public expectations 中的 public expectations（公众预期） 原文没有——末段谈的是合作应超越\"科研传播\"功能，与公众预期无关；go beyond 一 词制造了与正确项的伪同义陷阱。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"will intensify interdisciplinary competition 中 competition（竞争）与原文方向相反 ——原文末段主张的是双方合作加深、共同探索，而非把跨学科推向竞争。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"The reach of art-science tie-ups needs to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication ↔ should do more than communicating science participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other ↔ should do more than communicating science 预判要求选\"应超出科研传播之外做更多\"，should do more than communicating science 在情态、超越关系、科学传播三要素上严格对应作者主张句。"},"D":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"are becoming more popular than before 只对应末段第一句 this trend is as strong as ever——但这是作者承认的事实背景，不是末段主张；题干问 author holds that， 应取主张而非背景。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 In the last paragraph, the author holds that art-science collaborations ____ 问作 者在末段对话题持有的总观点，是末段层面的小主旨。","拆句：题干为待补全陈述句，主干 the author holds that art-science collaborations ____，that 引导宾语从句作 holds 的宾语，从句主语为 art-science collaborations，谓语由四个选项 延续；In the last paragraph 是地点状语。"]

questions.content: The personal grievance provisions of the ERA are intended to____
questions.options_json: {"A": "punish dubious corporate practices.", "B": "improve traditional hiring procedures.", "C": "exempt employers from certain duties.", "D": "protect the rights of ordinary workers."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"punish dubious corporate practices 谈「惩罚可疑企业行为」，但原文只说该条款 prevent…firing without good cause，是约束而非惩罚，且对象是 dismissal 行为而非 泛 corporate practices。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"improve traditional hiring procedures 谈「改良招聘流程」，但 dismissals must be justified 与 guard the jobs of ordinary workers from \"unjustified dismissals\" 全部 围绕解雇，不涉及招聘。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"exempt employers from certain duties 是「免除雇主义务」，但条款做的恰恰相反 ——给雇主加上 show cause 与 procedurally fair 两道义务（Employers must both show cause and act in a procedurally fair way）。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"guard the jobs of ordinary workers ↔ protect the rights of ordinary workers ordinary workers ↔ ordinary workers 预判要的是「保护普通工人」，D 项 protect the rights of ordinary workers 在受益对 象与立法目的两点上都与定位句对应，是唯一在两点上全等的选项。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 The personal grievance provisions of the ERA are intended to____ 问的是「被设 计来做什么」这一客观事实，没有 infer/imply 字样。","拆句：The personal grievance provisions of the ERA are intended to____ 主干是 provisions are intended to do sth，被动语态＋不定式，选项就是这个不定式的内容。结构无陷阱。","定位：Personal grievance procedures were designed to guard the jobs of ordinary workers from \"unjustified dismissals\". 人事申诉程序的设立目的，是保护普通工人的岗位免遭「不公正解雇」。"]

questions.content: It can be learned from Paragraph 3 that the provisions may____
questions.options_json: {"A": "hinder business development.", "B": "undermine managers' authority.", "C": "affect the public image of the firms.", "D": "worsen labor-management relations."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance ↔ hinder business development create difficulties for businesses ↔ hinder business development 预判要的是「拖累企业」，A 项正是把 handbrake 比喻去掉、把 productivity 上位为 business development 的标准推断题答案。"},"B":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"undermine managers' authority 谈「削弱管理者权威」，但本段说的是「无法解雇差 管理者」，受影响的是企业／老板的解雇权，不是管理者自己的权威。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"affect the public image of the firms 谈「影响企业公众形象」，但第 3 段只谈生产 率、绩效、业务成败，未涉及「公众形象」维度。"},"D":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"worsen labor-management relations 谈「恶化劳资关系」，但第 3 段对比的是「差 管理者 vs 好管理者」和「普通工人岗位保留 vs 丢失」，并未涉及劳资双方对立关系。"}}

questions.content: Which of the following measures would the Productivity Commission support?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Imposing reasonable wage restraints.", "B": "Enforcing employment protection laws.", "C": "Limiting the powers of business owners.", "D": "Dismissing poorly performing managers."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"Imposing reasonable wage restraints 谈「合理薪酬管制」，但 P5 委员会的归因落在 「管理能力」而非「管理者薪酬」上，没有任何句子支持工资管制立场。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"Enforcing employment protection laws 谈「加强用工保护法」，但全文（含 P5）的 论点恰恰是这类法律 act as a constraint on firm productivity，委员会立场必然与「加 强它」相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"Limiting the powers of business owners 谈「限制企业主权力」，但全文都在说应给 企业主松绑（解雇差管理者的权），委员会自然不会支持反向限权。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"the low quality of managerial capabilities ↔ Dismissing poorly performing managers as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record ↔ Dismissing poorly performing managers 预判要的是「换掉差管理者」，D 项 Dismissing poorly performing managers 是把 诊断结论变成对症措施的唯一选项。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：Which of the following measures would the Productivity Commission support? 原文 只点出该机构对生产率低的归因，「会支持哪条措施」需要由归因反推一步。","拆句：Which of the following measures would the Productivity Commission support? 是 Which + 名词 + would + 主语 + 动词 的虚拟语气问句；would 提示推断、support 是立 场动词，结构简洁无陷阱。","定位：the Productivity Commission singled out the low quality of managerial capabilities as a cause of the country's poor productivity growth record. 生产率委员会单独点名「管理能力低下」是新西兰生产率增长记录差的一大成因。"]

questions.content: What might be an effect of ERA's unjustified dismissal procedures?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Highly paid managers lose their jobs.", "B": "Employees suffer from salary cuts.", "C": "Society sees a rise in overall well-being.", "D": "Employers need to hire new staff."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"Highly paid managers lose their jobs 谈「高薪管理者丢工作」，但原文恰恰说这类 条款让差管理者难以被解雇 constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high- earning managers，方向相反。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"therefore on workers' wages ↔ Employees suffer from salary cuts firms pay staff less ↔ Employees suffer from salary cuts 预判要的是「工资被压低」，B 项 Employees suffer from salary cuts 在 P5 与 P6 都 有直接原文支撑，是唯一一项被原文两次明示的后果。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"Society sees a rise in overall well-being 谈「社会整体福祉上升」，但 Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall well-being 明说是 hamper（损害），方向相反。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"Employers need to hire new staff 谈「雇主需要招新人」，但 employers are more cautious about hiring new staff 说的恰是雇主更不愿招人，方向相反。"}}

questions.content: It can be inferred that the "high-income threshold" in Australia____
questions.options_json: {"A": "has secured managers' earnings.", "B": "has produced undesired results.", "C": "is beneficial to business owners.", "D": "is difficult to put into practice"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"has secured managers' earnings 谈「保住了管理者的收入」，但 P8 只说门槛划定 了保护边界，未谈管理者收入是否被保障；况且该门槛针对的是雇佣保护，不针对薪酬 本身。"},"B":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"has produced undesired results 谈「产生了不良后果」，但 P8 对澳大利亚做法是中 性陈述其机制；唯一被作者评价为「不良」的是新西兰 2016 年那次失败的 Bill（the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy）。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"excluding employees earning above a specified \"high-income threshold\" from the protection of its unfair dismissal laws ↔ is beneficial to business owners constraining firms from firing poorly performing, high-earning managers is a handbrake on boosting productivity and overall performance ↔ is beneficial to business owners 预判要的是「利好企业主」，C 项是唯一同时被定位句机制和全文论点链双重支撑的 选项。"},"D":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"is difficult to put into practice 谈「难以落地」，但澳大利亚的门槛是已经在用的现行 做法（Australia deals with the unjustified dismissal paradox by excluding 用一般 现在时陈述），无落地难的暗示；新西兰版本才被评为 unwieldy。"}}

questions.content: The example of organic eggs is used in Paragraph 4 to suggest____

questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文 there were similar doubts about probiotics and plant-based meats 中的 doubts 是对益生菌和植物肉的怀疑，且这些怀疑已被证伪——doubts 是被反驳的对 象。选项 doubts over natural feeds 把怀疑对象偷换为 natural feeds（天然饲料）， 原文从未提及。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"段落基调全是「从小众走向沃尔玛」「成为超市主要品类」「打开闸门」，全部为成功 叙事；选项 the setbacks in the egg industry（蛋业受挫）与全段基调相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"If the sustainable-egg rollout is successful, it could open the floodgates for regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond ↔ the potential of regenerative products regenerative beef, broccoli, and beyond ↔ regenerative products 预判「再生类产品有潜力」与 the potential of regenerative products 完全对应；只 有 C 抓住了例证服务的真正论点。"},"D":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"原文功劳归于产品本身和消费偏好转变，沃尔玛只是渠道结果，并未论及超市做了什么 营销；选项 the promotional success of supermarkets 把主语从「产品」偷换成「超 市的营销」。"}}

questions.content: It can be learned from the last paragraph that young people____

questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文说年轻人 absolutely altering the food chain（正在彻底改变食物链），即正在主 动改变饮食；选项 are reluctant to change their diet 与之方向完全相反。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"younger generations are more concerned about climate change ↔ are likely to buy climate-friendly eggs the same consumers paying more for premium attributes...will embrace sustainability ↔ climate-friendly eggs B 正好把「关心气候 + 愿为环保付钱」推到「会买气候友好蛋」，恰好一步、未跨步， 与预判完全契合。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文谈的是 concerned about climate change 和 wanting to signal their desire to protect the environment——动机是环保关切与价值观表达，不是 curious（好奇）。 新食品的「新颖性」原文未涉。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文末段聚焦消费者动机与代际差异，不评年轻人对「农业进步」的反应；amazed 这 种「惊叹」情绪也未出现。"}}
