questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文支持方谈的是\"真草也有代价\"，从未提及\"需要降低人造草坪的成本\"；lower the costs of fake grass 在文中无对应。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol ↔ the disadvantages of growing real grass real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments ↔ growing real grass 支持方所列的真草维护成本与环境代价，正是 the disadvantages of growing real grass 的具象化，与预判一致，锁 B。"},"C":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"题干问的是支持方\"指出了什么\"，选项却给\"养护人造草坪的方法\"。the way to take care of artificial lawns 与题问的核心错位。"},"D":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文说铺人造草坪的人会花约 500 英镑买 trees or shrubs for their garden, which provides habitat for insects，这是\"维护昆虫栖息\"的正面举证，而非\"昆虫栖息地保护 面临的挑战\"。选项把这种支持举证扭曲成\"挑战\"。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 supporters of fake grass point out 问的是支持方在第 4 段所列的具体观点，按细节 题处理。","拆句：In Paragraph 4, supporters of fake grass point out_____. 主干是 \"supporters point out X\"，In Paragraph 4 是状语，结构无难点。","定位：However, supporters of fake grass point out that there is also an environmental impact with natural lawns, which need mowing and therefore usually consume electricity or petrol. The industry also points out that real grass requires considerable amounts of water, weed killer or other treatments and that people who lay fake grass tend to use their garden more. 然而，人造草坪的支持者指出，天然草坪也有环境代价——它需要修剪，因而通常要耗电或 耗汽油。行业也指出，真草需要大量水、除草剂或其他处理，而铺设人造草坪的人往往会更 多地使用自家花园。"]

questions.content: What would the government do with regard to artificial grass?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Urge legislation to restrict its use.", "B": "Take measures to guarantee its quality.", "C": "Remind its users to obey existing rules.", "D": "Replace it with sustainable alternatives."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"Urge legislation to restrict its use. 与原文 no plans to ban the use of artificial grass 及 rather than legislating on such matters 正相反。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"Take measures to guarantee its quality. 涉及\"保证产品质量\"，原文政府表态从未涉及 人造草坪产品的质量管控。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage ↔ Remind its users to obey existing rules. prefer to help people and organisations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters ↔ Remind its users C 既反映\"政府选择引导而非立法\"，又反映\"要求使用者守现行规则\"，与定位句和预判完 全一致。"},"D":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"Replace it with sustainable alternatives. 借 consider sustainable alternatives 的眼 熟造势，但原文只是\"鼓励公共部门考虑可持续替代方案\"，并未说政府要替换掉 artificial grass。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 What would the government do with regard to artificial grass? 问的是政府针对 人造草坪要采取的行动，是对原文政府表态的复述，按细节题处理。","拆句：What would the government do with regard to artificial grass? 是 wh- 一般疑问句， with regard to 引导话题状语\"就……而言\"，无理解陷阱。","定位：We prefer to help people and organisations make the right choice rather than legislating on such matters. However, the use of artificial grass must comply with the legal and policy safeguards in place to protect biodiversity and ensure sustainable drainage, while measures such as the strengthened biodiversity duty should serve to encourage public authorities to consider sustainable alternatives. 我们更愿意帮助公众和组织做出正确选择，而不是就此类事项立法。但是，使用人造草坪必 须遵守现行的、用以保护生物多样性与确保可持续排水的法律与政策保障；同时，诸如强化 的生物多样性义务等措施应当推动公共部门考虑可持续的替代方案。"]

questions.content: What problem are U.S. national parks faced with?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Decline of business profits.", "B": "Inadequate commercialization.", "C": "Lack of transportation services.", "D": "Poorly maintained infrastructure."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文从未说公园本身利润下滑，businesses in the parks hand over, on average, only about 5% of their revenues 谈的是企业上缴比例低，非公园利润下降，Decline of business profits 既偷换对象（企业 vs 公园）又无中生有「下降」一说。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文明确反对增加商业化（increased privatization would certainly undercut one of the major reasons），Inadequate commercialization 却暗示「商业化不够」是问题 ——与作者立场完全相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"原文 Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling 列举的是整个基础设施集群，Lack of transportation services 只截取了 roads/trails，且把它们偷换为「交通服务缺失」，无中生有「服务」一说。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"other infrastructure are crumbling ↔ Poorly maintained infrastructure maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion ↔ Poorly maintained 预判「基础设施年久失修」与 Poorly maintained infrastructure 完全对应，且 D 的两 词都能在第二段找到原文支撑，故锁定 D。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：What problem are U.S. national parks faced with? 直接问国家公园面临的问题，要求在 原文中找到客观对应的表述，没有 infer/suggest/imply 等推断信号词。","拆句：题干 What problem are U.S. national parks faced with? 是常规的「What + 名词 + be + 主语 + 被动短语」结构，核心是 be faced with，意为「面临」，语序无倒装陷阱，无需 特别警惕。","定位：But the government is right about one thing: U.S. national parks are in crisis. Collectively, they have a maintenance backlog of more than $12 billion. Roads, trails, restrooms, visitor centers and other infrastructure are crumbling. 但政府说对了一件事：美国国家公园陷入危机。它们整体上有超过 120 亿美元的维护积压。 道路、步道、洗手间、游客中心和其他基础设施正在崩塌。"]

questions.content: Increased privatization of the campgrounds may_____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "spoil visitor experience", "B": "help preserve nature", "C": "bring operational pressure", "D": "boost visits to parks"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"undercut one of the major reasons why 300 million visitors come to the parks each year: to enjoy nature and get a break from the commercial drumbeat ↔ spoil visitor experience 预判「破坏游客游园体验」与 spoil visitor experience 一一对应：spoil 等值 undercut，visitor experience 概括 enjoy nature + get a break，故锁定 A。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文明确说私有化会破坏「享受自然」这一游园动机 undercut one of the major reasons，help preserve nature 反而把私有化说成保护自然，方向完全相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"全文未讨论「私有化是否给运营带来压力」，bring operational pressure 是凭空捏造 的后果。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文说私有化会破坏游客来公园的理由，逻辑上会减少游客或损害体验，boost visits to parks 说私有化会「促进游客访问」，方向反了。"}}

questions.content: According to Paragraph 5, most respondents in the survey would_____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "go to the national parks on a regular basis", "B": "advocate a bigger budget for the national parks", "C": "agree to pay extra for the national parks", "D": "support the national parks' recent reforms"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文只说受访者愿意付钱，并未提受访者是否「定期去公园」，go to the national parks on a regular basis 凭空给受访者添加了行为。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文是受访者「愿意自己掏钱」——通过缴税资助公园（would be willing to pay additional taxes），而 advocate a bigger budget for the national parks 把行为偷 换成「呼吁政府增加预算」——预算来自政府，与「自己缴税」是两件事。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"would be willing to pay additional taxes for the next 10 years ↔ agree to pay extra for the national parks to avoid any cuts to the national parks ↔ for the national parks 预判的「愿意多缴税保公园」三要素——意愿(willing/agree)、多付 (additional/extra)、目的(avoid cuts/for parks)——在 agree to pay extra for the national parks 中全部对应，故锁定 C。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文段未提及「公园近期有改革」一事，更未提受访者对此态度，support the national parks' recent reforms 凭空捏造。"}}

questions.content: The national parks are valuable in that they_____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "lead the way in tourism", "B": "have historical significance", "C": "sponsor research on climate", "D": "provide an income for the locals"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"原文 of course through tourism 只承认公园通过旅游创造价值，并未说「公园领跑/引 领旅游业」，lead the way in tourism 把「贡献价值」过度推断成「行业领跑」。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"help keep America's past alive ↔ have historical significance protect historical sites ↔ historical significance 预判中「保护历史遗址、让历史故事鲜活」这一价值项与 have historical significance 完全对应，且无其他选项能在段中找到完整支撑，故锁定 B。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文 positive impact on the climate through carbon sequestration 说公园通过碳 封存「对气候有正面影响」，而 sponsor research on climate 把「自身有正面影响」 偷换成「赞助气候研究」——一个是公园本身的生态功能，一个是资助科研活动，两 件事。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文 bring the stories of these places to life 和 through tourism 都没说公园「给当 地人提供收入」，provide an income for the locals 凭空把价值改造成「为当地居民 创收」。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：The national parks are valuable in that they_____. 问公园「在哪一点上有价值」，是问 某个具体方面，选项必是原文列举价值中的一项。","拆句：The national parks are valuable in that they_____. 是不完整陈述句；in that 在书面语中 等于 because，引导原因状语从句，主语 they 指代 the national parks，选项是公园做了 什么使它们有价值。","定位：The parks also help keep America's past alive, working with thousands of local jurisdictions around the country to protect historical sites and to bring the stories of these places to life. 公园还帮助保留美国的过去——与全国数千个地方司法管辖区合作，保护历史遗址，让这些 地方的故事鲜活起来。"]

questions.content: It can be concluded from the text that the national park system _____.
questions.options_json: {"A": "is able to cope with staff shortages", "B": "is able to meet visitors' demands", "C": "is in need of a new pricing policy", "D": "is in need of a funding increase"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"全文从未讨论公园「员工短缺」或「应对人手」，is able to cope with staff shortages 凭空捏造主题。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文以「拨款 20 年不涨、游客增 50%」论证系统已不堪重负 (Meanwhile, the number of annual visitors has increased by more than 50%)，is able to meet visitors' demands 反而说「能满足游客需求」，与全文论点方向相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"全文谈商业化、谈缴税意愿、谈拨款，但从未提「公园需要新的定价/票价政策」，is in need of a new pricing policy 凭空捏造。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"The real problem is that the parks have been chronically starved of funding ↔ is in need of a funding increase Congress allocates only $3 billion a year—an amount that has been flat since 2001 ↔ funding increase 预判「系统需要增加资金投入」与 is in need of a funding increase 一一对应，且 D 同时覆盖第二、五、七段的核心论断，是唯一覆盖全文主线的选项，故锁定 D。"}}

questions.content: The UK's exposure to fluctuating wood prices is a result of______.
questions.options_json: {"A": "the government's inaction on timber imports", "B": "inadequate investment in growing wood", "C": "the competition among timber traders at home", "D": "wood producers' motive to maximise profits"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文把价格波动归因于\"未投资本土\"，并未指责政府在进口管制上\"不作为\"；inaction on timber imports 把矛头转到 imports，与原文因果链脱节。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply ↔ inadequate investment in growing wood our domestic wood supply ↔ growing wood 预判的\"几十年未投资本土供应\"在 inadequate investment in growing wood 中以\"对 种树投资不足\"重述，主语指向、动作方向、否定语气完全一致，故选 B。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"competition among timber traders at home 在文本里找不到对应；原文谈的是与全 球争夺供应（fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises），不是 国内木材贸易商之间的竞争。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"wood producers' motive to maximise profits 把价格波动归咎于木材生产商追求利润 最大化；原文对\"producers' motive/profits\"完全没提，纯属强加。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 is a result of 直白追问原因，是原文中已明示因果关系的细节查找，未 含 infer/imply。","拆句：The UK's exposure to fluctuating wood prices is a result of______ 主语 The UK's exposure to fluctuating wood prices 较长，核心名词为 exposure；系动词 is + a result of 构成原因关系，空格处填名词性短语，无复杂结构。","定位：For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall. 几十年来我们没有承担起投资本土木材供应的责任，这使我们暴露在波动的价格之下，并在 全球需求上涨、本国供应下降之时争夺未来的木材供应。"]

questions.content: What does Goodall think the UK government should do?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Subsidise the building of low-carbon homes.", "B": "Pay greater attention to boosting rural economies.", "C": "Provide more support for productive tree planting.", "D": "Give priority to pursuing its net-zero strategy."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"Subsidise the building of low-carbon homes 把支持对象错配到\"低碳住宅的建造\"； 原文 ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes 只是说英国适 合种木材以建低碳住宅，Goodall 主张的是支持种树而非补贴建房。"},"B":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"Pay greater attention to boosting rural economies 把\"为农村经济带来收益\"当成 Goodall 的主张，但原文中 rural economies 只是 productive tree planting 的附带好 处之一，Goodall 真正呼吁的是支持 productive tree planting 本身。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies ↔ Provide more support for productive tree planting the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity ↔ Provide more support 预判的\"加大对生产性种树的支持\"在 Provide more support for productive tree planting 原词复现并精确对位，故选 C。"},"D":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"Give priority to pursuing its net-zero strategy 把\"净零战略\"升格为首要目标，原文只 说 contribute to the UK's net-zero strategy（有助于净零），未将其列为优先项； Goodall 的呼吁是\"land to also provide\"的并列诉求，而非排他优先。"}}

questions.content: Dugan thinks that the solution to the problems of crashes may lie in______.
questions.options_json: {"A": "upgrading self-driving vehicles", "B": "developing senior-friendly cars", "C": "renovating transport facilities", "D": "adjusting the age limit for drivers"}

questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有=造新挑战维度","explanation":"段 4 论述的是 FTC 权限（only act after the fact）和 app 上市速度，未提健康信息本 身的 complexity，The complexity of health information 是无中生有。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market ↔ The rapid increase in new health apps 预判 \"新 app 涌入速度太快\" 与 The rapid increase in new health apps 中 rapid increase 完全等价——速度快即增量多，原文与选项指同一现象。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念=移位+加修饰","explanation":"原文 initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts 中的 deceptive 是 FTC 法定可执法对象的描述，且无 subtle（微妙的）这一修饰；同时挑战不来自 \"deceptive 程度\" 而来自 \"app 上市速度\"。The subtle deceptiveness of health apps 把法律术语挪到挑战位置，并杜撰 subtle 一词。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有=蹭术语造新难点","explanation":"原文 unjustified consumer harm 是 FTC 法律条款里描述 \"不合理消费者损害\" 的术 语，并未讨论 \"评估损害的难度\"。The difficulty in assessing consumer harm 杜撰了 一个评估难度的新维度。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：What challenge is the FTC currently faced with 问具体面临的挑战内容，可在原文里找 到字面对应。","拆句：题干 What challenge is the FTC currently faced with 是疑问代词 What 作 challenge 的 修饰，be faced with 是被动短语 \"面临\"，结构常见，无陷阱。","定位：While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is. 尽管 FTC 正在竭尽所能确保这些 app 兑现对消费者关于敏感健康信息处置的承诺，但这些 健康 app 涌入市场的速度，显示出这一挑战何其巨大。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2024年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第86—117页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2024年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第1—721页；原文定位：While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is. 尽管 FTC 正在竭尽所能确保这些 app 兑现对消费者关于敏感健康信息处置的承诺，但这些 健康 app 涌入市场的速度，显示出这一挑战何其巨大。

questions.content: It can be learned from the last paragraph that health data protection______.
questions.options_json: {"A": "has been embraced by health app developers", "B": "has been a focus of federal policy-making", "C": "has encountered opposition in California", "D": "has gained legislative support in some states"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有=换主语角色","explanation":"段 5 通篇讨论联邦与州两级的立法情况，未提 health app developers 的态度；has been embraced by health app developers 是无中生有。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反=方向颠倒","explanation":"原文 comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term 明确联邦立法短期 unlikely，与 \"已成联邦政策制定焦点\" 方向相反，has been a focus of federal policy-making 与原文相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反=立场颠倒","explanation":"原文 California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts 明确加州在州一级 隐私保护中走在最前列，与 \"在加州遭遇反对\" 完全相反，has encountered opposition in California 与原文相反。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer- generated health data ↔ has gained legislative support in some states California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 ↔ legislative support Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation ↔ in some states 预判 \"州层面已有立法支持\" 与 has gained legislative support in some states 一一对 应：has gained 对应州层动作已发生，legislative support 对应四州的立法实证， some states 对应枚举的几个州，无溢出无遗漏。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：It can be learned from the last paragraph 的 \"can be learned\" 等价于 can be inferred，要求推断段意。","拆句：题干 It can be learned from the last paragraph that health data protection 是形式主 语 It + 被动 + that 引导真实主语从句，that 后接选项补全句子，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。","定位：As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation. 至于联邦立法的前景，评论人士认为短期内全面的联邦隐私立法不太可能。各州已开始自行 推出方案，加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。加州凭借 2018 年《加州消费者隐私法 案》一直走在州一级隐私保护的最前列。弗吉尼亚、科罗拉多和犹他也最近通过了州一级的 消费者数据隐私立法。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语二2024年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第86—117页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.
questions.evidence_note: PDF原解析：考研英语二2024年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第1—1017页；原文定位：As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation. 至于联邦立法的前景，评论人士认为短期内全面的联邦隐私立法不太可能。各州已开始自行 推出方案，加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。加州凭借 2018 年《加州消费者隐私法 案》一直走在州一级隐私保护的最前列。弗吉尼亚、科罗拉多和犹他也最近通过了州一级的 消费者数据隐私立法。

questions.content: The "rehearsal room" approach requires pupils to___________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "rewrite the lines from Shakespeare", "B": "watch RSC actors' performances", "C": "play the roles in Shakespeare", "D": "study drama under RSC artists"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"全文没有任何”重写/改写台词”的描述，rewrite 是凭空加上去的动作；这是利用题干” requires pupils to“求动作的预期，给一个看似合理但文中没有的动作。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"原文要求孩子\"act him out\"亲身演出，而 watch RSC actors’ performances 把动作 从\"演\"偷换成\"看\"——主动变被动，与原文意旨相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"the way actors work ↔ play the roles in Shakespeare if you act him out ↔ play the roles in Shakespeare 预判要的就是\"演\"，C 选项 play the roles in Shakespeare 直接对应\"演员工作方 式\"与\"act him out\"，是最干净的同义替换。"},"D":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"原文 RSC 是研究的委托方，不是教学执行方；孩子是被引导用\"演员方式\"工作，不 是\"在 RSC 艺术家手下学戏剧\"。该选项把研究合作关系夸大成”直接师从”。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 The \"rehearsal room\" approach requires pupils to___________. 是要求填具体做法的 不完整陈述句，没有 infer/suggest/imply 之类推断信号词，属于典型细节题。","拆句：题干 The \"rehearsal room\" approach requires pupils to___________. 是一个待补全的陈述 句，主语 The \"rehearsal room\" approach，谓语 requires，宾语 pupils，不定式 to ___ 是要填的部分，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。","定位：\"The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves,\" Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said. 皇家莎士比亚剧团（RSC，本研究的委托方）的 Jacqui O'Hanlon 说：\"这项研究表明，演 员的工作方式深深改变了孩子们使用语言的方式，也改变了他们对自己的认识。\""]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语一2025年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第39—51页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: "The research shows that the way actors work makes a big difference to the way children use language and also how they think about themselves," Jacqui O'Hanlon of the Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC), which commissioned the study, said.

questions.content: The study divided the pupils into two groups to find whether___________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "the change in instruction enhances learning outcomes", "B": "expanding vocabulary helps develop reading fluency", "C": "emotion affects understanding of sophisticated works", "D": "the classroom activity stimulates interest in the arts"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"a 30-minute drama-based activity ↔ the change in instruction The peer-reviewed results showed that the target group of pupils drew on a wider vocabulary, used words \"classed as more sophisticated or rarer\", and wrote at greater length. ↔ enhances learning outcomes 唯一变量是教学方式的改变，被观测的产出是写作/学习上的表现，A 选项把”变量→产 出”的因果检验完整覆盖，与预判一致。"},"B":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"扩展词汇是该实验的部分结果之一，不是分组想检验的初衷；而且 reading fluency \"阅 读流畅度\"原文从未提及，把写作产出偷换成阅读能力。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文 P6 的因果是\"戏剧化方法→情感素养→更好的写作\"，而 emotion affects understanding of sophisticated works 把方向反过来变成\"情感→对高级作品的理 解\"，且 sophisticated works 也偷换了原文 sophisticated words（高级用词）。"},"D":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"戏剧化活动在本研究中是\"手段\"（独立变量），不是要被检验的\"对艺术的兴趣\"这一结 果；arts 取自 P6 末尾的 embedding arts in education 的余韵，被强行嫁接到研究目 的上。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 The study divided the pupils into two groups to find whether___________. 问的是 分组实验本身要检验什么，可在原文中找到对应陈述，不需做跨段推断。","拆句：题干 The study divided the pupils into two groups to find whether___________. 中 to find whether 是目的状语，whether 引导宾语从句，从句内容正是要填的部分；理解关键 是看清”分组”是手段，”find whether ...“才是目的。","定位：They were split into target and control groups and asked to write, for example, a message in a bottle as Ferdinand after the shipwreck in *The Tempest*. The target group was given a 30- minute drama-based activity to accompany the passage. 他们被分成 target（实验）组和 control（对照）组，被要求以《暴风雨》中船难之后的 Ferdinand 身份写一封”漂流瓶里的信”。target 组额外获得了一个 30 分钟的戏剧化活动来 配合该段落。"]

questions.content: Control pupils' reliance on "desert island clichés" shows their ___________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "weakness in description", "B": "omission of small details", "C": "casual style of writing", "D": "preference for big words"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"relied on \"desert island clichés\" such as palm trees ↔ weakness in description target pupils were \"more expansive [giving a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions\"]] ↔ weakness in description 陈词滥调一词本身就是写作描述贫弱的标准外显，A 选项与预判完全吻合。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"control 组不是\"遗漏了小细节\"，而是\"画面单调\"；原文反差是\"狭窄 vs 宏阔\"，不是\"漏 vs 不漏\"；而且 small details 在原文没有任何对应。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"clichés 是明确负面的词，原文是在批评 control 组写作贫弱；casual style of writing 把这种负面评价淡化为\"随意的写作风格\"这一中性甚至略带褒义的描述，性质方向错。"},"D":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"preference for big words 描述的是\"偏爱大词\"——这正是 target 组的特征（words \"classed as more sophisticated or rarer\"），不是 control 组；而且 palm trees 显然 不是 big words。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 Control pupils' reliance on \"desert island clichés\" shows their ___________. 用 shows 把原文现象指向其反映的”特质”，需要从描写一步推到性质判断。","拆句：题干 Control pupils' reliance on \"desert island clichés\" shows their ___________. 主语是 动名词性短语 Control pupils' reliance on ... clichés，谓语 shows，宾语 their ___ 待填； 理解要点是 reliance on clichés“对陈词滥调的依赖”本身就是负面色彩，正确答案应延续这 一负面方向。","定位：The Time to Act study also found that while control pupils relied on \"desert island clichés\" such as palm trees, target pupils were \"more expansive [giving] a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions\". \"是时候行动\"研究还发现：control 组的学生只靠\"沙漠岛俗套\"（比如棕榈树）来写，而 target 组的学生\"更加宏阔，呈现出关于天空、大海与大气状况的更广阔画面\"。"]

questions.content: What can promote children's emotional literacy according to O'Hanlon?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Writing in an imaginative manner.", "B": "Identifying with literary characters.", "C": "Drawing inspiration from nature.", "D": "Concentrating on real-life situations."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"imaginative manner 是写作方式的形容，但 O'Hanlon 给的因不是\"用想象力写\"，而 是\"代入别人去想象\"；imaginative manner 只描述了想象这一表层动作，没有抓住”代 入他人\"这一关键机制。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"put yourself in different shoes ↔ Identifying with literary characters. [target children put themselves in the shoes of a literary character and express that character's emotion]] ↔ Identifying with literary characters. 原文反复强调”穿别人的鞋”+“代入文学角色”，B 选项用 identifying with literary characters 把这两层意思合二为一，与预判精准吻合。"},"C":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"Drawing inspiration from nature 取自 P5 a broader picture of the sky, the sea and the atmospheric conditions，那段讨论的是写作描述力，与情感素养的成因无关； O'Hanlon 没把情感素养归因于自然。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"O'Hanlon 强调的是\"代入别人/角色\"，与 Concentrating on real-life situations\"专注 于真实生活情境\"方向相反——真实生活情境恰恰是 control 组的反应（[control pupils imagine how they themselves would react to being shipwrecked]]）。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 What can promote children's emotional literacy according to O'Hanlon? 限定到 O'Hanlon 的原话，需要在文中找她的引语，属人物观点细节题。","拆句：题干 What can promote children's emotional literacy according to O'Hanlon? 是一个 wh-疑问句，主语是疑问代词 What，谓语 can promote，according to O'Hanlon 是观点 来源状语；理解关键是绑定 O'Hanlon 这一信源，不能用全文其他来源的描述代替。","定位：She added: \"The emotional understanding was very evident and it is probably related to the [rehearsal room process] where you are used to trying to imagine your way through. They were comfortable in describing different emotional states and part of what you do in drama is put yourself in different shoes.\" 她补充道：“情感理解非常明显，这很可能与”排练室式过程”有关——在那种过程中，你习惯 于一路靠想象去走通。他们能从容地描述各种不同的情绪状态，而戏剧的一部分就是把自己 放进不同的鞋里（换位）。”"]

questions.content: It can be inferred from the last paragraph that ___________.

questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads ↔ played a part in the fight against illegal file-sharing 原文事实 \"Netflix 帮助压制以文件上传为主的盗版\" 一步推 \"Netflix 在打击非法文件分 享中扮演了角色\"，正是 played a part in the fight against illegal file-sharing。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"reaped benefits from the war with digital pirates 是 \"Netflix 从与盗版的对战中获 利\"；但原文里获利的是盗版方 (上一段 unintended winners… pirates)，Netflix 们反 而 has struggled to turn a profit in streaming，正反角色颠倒。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"promised to become big job creators in the US 谈的是 Netflix 们承诺创造大量岗 位；第三段只提 some 250,000 jobs 的损失，且是盗版造成的、不是 Netflix 承诺的就 业贡献。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"used to collaborate with file-uploading platforms 说 Netflix 曾与文件上传平台合 作；但定位句 helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads 明示 Netflix 是 \"遏制\" 文件上传盗版，而非合作。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 It can be learned that streamers like Netflix ________ 使用 It can be learned 引 导，要求由原文事实出发做一步合理推论。","拆句：It can be learned that streamers like Netflix ________ 是 It can be learned that 引导宾 语从句的不完整结构，主语 streamers like Netflix 在从句内，空格补从句谓语；like 在这 里是介词 \"诸如\"，不是动词，基础薄弱考生易误读为 \"喜欢\"，须留意。","定位：Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads. 起初，像 Netflix 这样的合法在线生意的崛起，其实帮助遏制了数字盗版，而当时的盗版主 要靠文件上传维系。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语一2025年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第68—82页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads.

questions.options_json: {"A": "was denied cooperation by Silicon Valley", "B": "led a national protest against online piracy", "C": "was urged to form an enforcement task force", "D": "failed to win support from local authorities"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy ↔ was denied cooperation by Silicon Valley MPA 推动立法时与硅谷未达共识、立法泡汤，这件事的最经济解读就是硅谷拒绝合作， 正对应 was denied cooperation by Silicon Valley。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"led a national protest against online piracy 说 MPA 领导了全国抗议；原文只提推动 legislation in Congress 与成立 Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE)，与 \"全国抗议\" 无关。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"was urged to form an enforcement task force 说 MPA 是 \"被敦促\" 才组建 ACE；但 原文 In 2017 the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE) 是 MPA 自发组建，并无任何 \"被外界催促\" 的描述。"},"D":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"failed to win support from local authorities 把不合作方说成 local authorities；原文 里不合作方是 Silicon Valley，且 about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities 反而显示 ACE 与各地警方是合作关系。"}}

questions.content: According to Hawley, digital piracy ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "cannot be checked in spite of new legislation", "B": "will possibly overwhelm legitimate streamers", "C": "is unlikely to diminish in the near future", "D": "has been underestimated by some analysts"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"cannot be checked in spite of new legislation 加进 \"in spite of new legislation\"， 把 a 2020 federal law 拉来作 \"对照失败\" 的对象；但 Hawley 的话只谈走势与共识， 并未否定立法的效果，是替 Hawley 替别人答非所问。"},"B":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"will possibly overwhelm legitimate streamers 把 \"压垮正版流媒体\" 这一结论塞给 Hawley；他只谈走势与共识，并未做出 \"盗版会压垮正版\" 这种更进一步的预测。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline ↔ is unlikely to diminish in the near future emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027 ↔ is unlikely to diminish in the near future Hawley 明说 \"何时开始下降\" 都无共识，连乐观面也只是 2027 年才能趋稳；由此一步 推 \"短期内盗版不太可能减少\"，正对 is unlikely to diminish in the near future。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"has been underestimated by some analysts 说一些分析师低估了盗版；原文里 Hawley 自己就是分析师，并未评价 \"其他分析师有没有低估\"，无任何文本依据。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 According to Hawley, digital piracy ________ 复述特定人物的观点，属事实型细 节题。","拆句：According to Hawley, digital piracy ________ 主语 digital piracy，谓语空缺；四个选项均 为含情态动词或被动的复合谓语，特别注意 is unlikely to diminish 是 \"不太可能减少\"，双 重含蓄否定，考生易误判为肯定。","定位：While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline. 尽管有人乐观地认为，新的对策与最佳实践或许会让盗版在 2027 年趋于平稳，但各方对于 盗版何时开始下降仍无共识。"]
questions.answer_source_note: 用户提供并认可的真题答案；考研英语一2025年真题及答案解析（整卷）.pdf，PDF第68—82页逐题【答案】。
questions.source_quote: While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline.

questions.content: Which of the following is emphasized in the text?
questions.options_json: {"A": "The need to coordinate anti-piracy action.", "B": "The criminal nature of copyright violation.", "C": "The prospect of eliminating online piracy.", "D": "The economic harm from illegal streaming."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"The need to coordinate anti-piracy action. 把第四段 failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley 的局部信息当全文主旨；文 章只在第四段顺带提了一次共识失败，其余段落并不围绕 \"协调\" 展开。"},"B":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"The criminal nature of copyright violation. 只能对应第四段 This is organized crime 与第五段 a serious crime 两处，文章重点不是定罪、而是算账。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"The prospect of eliminating online piracy. 暗示文章在谈消除盗版的前景；但末段 no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline 明白说没人知 道何时开始下降，全文对 \"消除\" 持谨慎甚至悲观态度。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions ↔ The economic harm from illegal streaming. piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs ↔ The economic harm from illegal streaming. legitimate US streaming services' cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years ↔ The economic harm from illegal streaming. 全文反复出现的不是 \"如何打击\"、不是 \"是否犯罪\"、也不是 \"能否消灭\"，而是 \"损失了 多少钱、多少岗位\"，The economic harm from illegal streaming. 正是这条主线的最 简概括。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 Which of the following is emphasized in the text? 不限定段落、问全文强调，是典 型主旨题。","拆句：Which of the following is emphasized in the text? 是疑问句，问 \"以下哪项被本文强 调\"；emphasize 是 \"反复强调\"，比 mention 强、比 prove 弱，正确项必须是文中多处回 扣的内容，不是只出现一次。"]

questions.content: The author mentions the artifacts from the past to ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "introduce the collection of antiques", "B": "contrast them with everyday items", "C": "bring up the issue of preservation", "D": "comment on their historical value"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"把例子当主题的典型干扰","explanation":"introduce the collection of antiques 把作者引子里 antiques store 当成主题；可作者 讲古董店只是借场景举例，全文真正主题是保存，不是收藏。"},"B":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"contrast them with everyday items 提到的「与日常物对比」原文从未出现，第一段 只把 artifacts 视为留存样本，没有任何 everyday items 出现。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible. ↔ bring up the issue of preservation 预判「引出保存议题」与 bring up the issue of preservation 在动词（引出 vs bring up）与宾语（议题 vs the issue of preservation）上一一对应，直接锁定 C。"},"D":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"comment on their historical value 谈历史价值；原文 Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral 讨论的是「为何能留存」，不是「它们有多少历史价值」。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 The author mentions the artifacts from the past to 用「mention X to do」结 构，问的是举例服务于哪一个论点。","拆句：题干 The author mentions the artifacts from the past to 是一个待补全句，主干为 The author mentions ... to + 选项动词原形，to 引出目的状语，无陷阱。","定位：Yet these objects aren't truly ephemeral, because they're still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they're tangible. 然而这些东西并非真正转瞬即逝，因为几十年甚至几百年后它们依然在这里。为什么？因为 它们是有形的。"]

questions.content: Compared with digital objects, tangible artifacts ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "are less subject to their creators' neglect", "B": "convey information in a more direct way", "C": "require more intentional preservation", "D": "are less likely to suffer serious damage"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"are less subject to their creators' neglect 称有形物较少被创作者忽视；原文 often despite their original creators' neglect 恰恰说有形物常在创作者疏忽下仍然留存，并 未说创作者对它们更上心。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. ↔ convey information in a more direct way 其它三项谈的是 neglect/preservation/damage，全在「保存难度」维度，与定位句 「传递机制」不在同一语义场，故 B 是唯一与预判匹配的。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"require more intentional preservation 称有形物需要更刻意的保存；原文 At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation 恰说创作时没 有刻意保存的努力，与选项相反。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"are less likely to suffer serious damage 说有形物不易受损；原文未在「受损程度」上 比较有形与数字，第二段谈的是创作者保存意图与留存机会，不涉及损伤难度。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干 Compared with digital objects, tangible artifacts 不含 infer/imply 等推断信号， 问的是作者直接陈述的对比属性。","拆句：题干 Compared with digital objects, tangible artifacts 中 Compared with digital objects 是过去分词短语作状语，逻辑主语是 tangible artifacts，主干仍是 tangible artifacts + 选项谓语。","定位：The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. 物件本身就是承载并传递信息的媒介。"]

questions.content: According to Paragraph 3, librarians' work may result in ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "oversupply of materials", "B": "undervaluation of libraries", "C": "researchers' underperformance", "D": "users' overreliance on technology"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"oversupply of materials 指材料供过于求；原文 embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems 谈的是「检索难」（大海捞 针），而非数量上的供过于求。且该句在第二段，不属于 Q38 限定的 Paragraph 3。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"libraries are less vital for researchers today ↔ undervaluation of libraries 预判「让用户贬低图书馆的价值」与 undervaluation of libraries 在主体（libraries） 和动作（贬低/低估）上完全对应，因此锁 B。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"researchers' underperformance 称研究者表现不佳；第三段只说用户「认为图书馆不 重要」，未评价研究者本身的表现高低。"},"D":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"users' overreliance on technology 把矛头对准「用户过度依赖科技」；原文谈的是用 户因此低估图书馆的价值，而不是评价用户依赖科技本身是好是坏。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：librarians' work may result in 问的是行为带来的具体结果，是段内客观信息的直接转述。","拆句：题干 According to Paragraph 3, librarians' work may result in 主干 work may result in + 选项名词性短语；情态动词 may 仅是缓和语气，不是推断信号。","定位：Librarians' selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cell phone and saying, \"it's all in here\" as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today. 图书馆员的无私付出反过来会害了我们——用户举起手机说「一切都在这里」，以此为据声 称图书馆对今日的研究者已没那么重要。"]

questions.content: The "ZIP disk" is cited as an example to show ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "the hazard of retrieving files through unusual means", "B": "the infeasibility of constantly migrating digital assets", "C": "the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats", "D": "the inconvenience of storing information on analog devices"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"the hazard of retrieving files through unusual means 暗示作者警告「用非常手段取 文件存在危险」；原文只问 how do I get the files off this，没有提及 unusual means 或 hazard 这类延伸。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"the infeasibility of constantly migrating digital assets 说「持续迁移数字资产不可 行」；原文 Without constant migration of digital assets 把持续迁移视为解决办法而 非「不可行」，逻辑相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless. ↔ the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? ↔ the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats C 项 obsolete formats 与原文 a format becomes obsolete 直接对应，losing information 又能解释「文件取不出」的具体场景，是预判到答案的直接落点。"},"D":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"the inconvenience of storing information on analog devices 把不便归到 analog devices；ZIP disk 是数字载体（digital），原文也专谈数字物的脆弱，张冠李戴。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：The \"ZIP disk\" is cited as an example to show 直接点明本题问举例的目的。","拆句：题干 The \"ZIP disk\" is cited as an example to show 中被动语态 is cited 的施事是作者， to show 引出目的状语，主语 ZIP disk 加引号强调原词出现。","定位：As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless. Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? 随着技术演进、格式过时，存储物件便变得毫无用处。你是否曾无助地盯着一张 ZIP 盘心 想：要怎么把里面的文件取出来？"]

questions.content: Which of the following statements best summarizes the text?
questions.options_json: {"A": "Hard work should be done to preserve artifacts.", "B": "Contributions of librarians should be recognized.", "C": "Accessing databases is essential to researchers.", "D": "Keeping digital historical records is a challenge."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"Hard work should be done to preserve artifacts. 用泛泛的 artifacts 代替「数字记 录」，没有点出数字时代这个核心矛盾；且文章主线不是泛泛号召 hard work，而是揭 示数字保存的难处与图书馆员角色。"},"B":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"Contributions of librarians should be recognized. 只截取第三段「图书馆员被低估」 一面，没覆盖第四段 ZIP disk 例子与第五段表态；文章主旨是数字记录保存的挑战，图 书馆员的贡献只是论证中的一环。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"Accessing databases is essential to researchers. 谈数据库访问的必要性；原文 universality of access 只是作为「用户低估图书馆」的引子，文章并未论证数据库访问 对研究者的必要性。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog ↔ Keeping digital historical records is a challenge. I'd be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists ↔ Keeping digital historical records is a challenge. D 项把全文「难」+ 「可努力」的态度合在「a challenge」一个词里，覆盖 P2–P5 全 部内容，且与作者既忧又持希望的口吻一致。"}}

questions.content: According to Paragraph 1, the practice of tipping in the U.S. ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "was regarded as a sign of generosity", "B": "was considered essential for waiters", "C": "was a way of rewarding diligence", "D": "was optional in most businesses"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文从未把小费描述为a sign of generosity（慷慨的象征），段中只讲“付给以小费为 主要收入者”的做法，与慷慨无关。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"earning most of their income via tips ↔ was considered essential for waiters U.S. customers historically tipped ↔ was considered 预判“小费对低薪服务员是必需收入”，四个选项中只有was considered essential for waiters准确对应“essential（必需）+ waiters（服务员）”，故锁 B。"},"C":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"was a way of rewarding diligence（奖励勤勉）对应的是reward high-quality service（奖励优质服务）的概念，那是第 2 段对“过去事后小费”的描述，与 Q21 限定 的Paragraph 1不符；且 diligence（勤勉）≠ high-quality service（优质服务）。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文说小费集中给“以小费为主要收入”的工种（如低于最低工资的服务员），暗示在那些 工种里给小费几乎是惯例、并非可有可无；was optional in most businesses反过来说 “在大多数行业里可给可不给”，与“传统上限定特定行业”的事实相反，且 most businesses 范围被放大。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干According to Paragraph 1, the practice of tipping in the U.S.显式指段，问的是该 段对小费做法的客观陈述，不带 infer / suggest / imply。","拆句：According to Paragraph 1, the practice of tipping in the U.S. ________. 主句是 the practice of tipping in the U.S. + 空格谓语；According to Paragraph 1 是状语，限定信 息来源；选项是对主语 the practice of tipping 的谓语补全，理解上无陷阱。","定位：U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage. 美国顾客历来只给那些他们认为大部分收入来源于小费的人付小费，比如时薪低于最低工资 的餐厅服务员。"]

questions.source_quote: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.

questions.content: Compared with tips in the past, today's tips ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "are paid much less frequently", "B": "are less often requested in advance", "C": "have less to do with service quality", "D": "contribute less to workers' income"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文没说今天小费“被支付的频次”比过去少；恰恰相反，第 4 段tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services暗示场合更多了。are paid much less frequently在频率维度上无原文支撑。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand明确说“事前 请求小费越来越普遍”，所以今天 in advance 的小费请求是更多而非更少；are less often requested in advance恰好把方向写反。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms ↔ have less to do with service quality That timing could reward high-quality service ↔ service quality 预判差异维度是“与服务质量挂钩程度下降”，四个选项中只有have less to do with service quality精确命中这一维度，故锁 C。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers明确说今天的小费正在“更多地”补贴低薪工人的收入； contribute less to workers' income反向缩小其贡献，与原文相反。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干Compared with tips in the past, today's tips要求找两个时点之间的差异，是对原文 显式对比的复盘，非推断。","拆句：Compared with tips in the past, today's tips ________. Compared with tips in the past 是过去分词短语作状语，逻辑主语是 today's tips；主语 today's tips 后接空缺谓语，由选 项补全；无从句、无否定，结构平铺。","定位：Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip. Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered. That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it. 今天的小费请求往往已不再与过去决定何时及如何付小费的薪资和服务规范相挂钩。过去顾 客几乎总是在享受完服务后才付小费，比如餐毕、剪完头发或披萨送达之后；这种时机本可 奖励优质服务并激励工人提供优质服务。"]

questions.source_quote: Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip. Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered. That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.

questions.content: Tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services as a result of ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "the advancement of technology", "B": "the desire for income increase", "C": "the diversification of business", "D": "the emergence of tipflation"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"The prevalence of digital payment devices ↔ the advancement of technology has made it easier to ask customers for a tip ↔ the advancement of technology 预判原因为“数字支付普及”，A 选项以“technology 进步”作为更宽泛但精准包含原因的 上位概念，与原文因果完全吻合，故锁 A。"},"B":{"trapType":"张冠李戴","explanation":"the desire for income increase（加薪诉求）对应的是第 7 段to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation，那是雇主“屈从于”小费蔓延的原因，而非小 费蔓延到新型服务的直接原因；段位与因果链都不对。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文从未提到“商业多元化 / 业态多元化”导致小费请求扩散；the diversification of business是无中生有的因。"},"D":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文This increase is sometimes called tipflation把 tipflation 定义为“小费比例不断上 涨的预期”，是“小费蔓延”现象的结果或同伴现象，而非其原因；the emergence of tipflation把结果当原因，因果倒置。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干as a result of问的是已被原文用 helps explain why 这类显式因果句写出的原因，属于 事实定位，不是推断。","拆句：Tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services as a result of ________. 主句 Tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services 用现在进行时表趋势；as a result of 引介动名词宾语（由选项补全），是固定因果短语；句式平铺无陷阱。","定位：The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services. 数字支付设备的普及让向顾客索取小费变得更容易了。这有助于解释为什么小费请求正在蔓 延到新型服务里。"]

questions.source_quote: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services.

questions.content: The movement toward no-tipping services was intended to ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "promote consumption", "B": "enrich income sources", "C": "maintain reasonable prices", "D": "guarantee income fairness"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文没说该运动旨在promote consumption（促进消费）；提价反而可能抑制消费，与 原文意图不符。"},"B":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"enrich income sources（丰富收入来源）问的是收入“多样化”，但原文目的是“公平”而 非“多样”——禁止小费、单一靠工资恰恰是减少而非丰富收入来源；与目的相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文明确说该运动选择了increased prices（提价），并不是为了维持合理价格； maintain reasonable prices与原文做法相反。"},"D":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages ↔ guarantee income fairness all employees ↔ income fairness 预判目的是“工资公平”，四选项中 D 直接用“guarantee income fairness”复刻原文 ensure...fair wages，是最直接的同义替换，故锁 D。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：原文用 To ensure that ... 直接交代了该运动的目的，题干intended to问的就是这一显式目 的，属细节定位。","拆句：The movement toward no-tipping services was intended to ________. 主语 The movement toward no-tipping services 后接被动谓语 was intended to + 不定式（由选 项补全 do 动词）；toward 介词短语作主语后置定语；结构平铺无陷阱。","定位：To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out. 为了确保所有员工都拿到公平的工资，一些餐厅禁止小费并提高了菜价，但这场无小费服务 运动已大体熄火。"]

questions.source_quote: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.

questions.content: It can be learned from the last paragraph that tipping ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "is becoming a burden for customers", "B": "helps encourage quality service", "C": "is vital to business development", "D": "reflects the need to reduce prices"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often ↔ is becoming a burden for customers tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous ↔ is becoming a burden for customers 预判方向是“小费成顾客负担”，四选项中只有 A 用“burden for customers”准确接住末 段对顾客 frustrated + coercive 的情绪 / 评价聚合，故锁 A。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文often completely dissociated from service quality明确说小费“已与服务质量完 全脱钩”，自然不再激励优质服务；helps encourage quality service与该结论相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"末段没说小费对business development（商业发展）至关重要；段中讨论的是顾客感受 与作者评价，与企业发展无关。"},"D":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"末段提的是“to increase employee wages without raising prices”——只是雇主不想 涨价，并未上升到“需要降价”的结论；reflects the need to reduce prices在“不涨”基础 上多走一步到“要降”，属过度推断。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：题干It can be learned from the last paragraph that tipping含 It can be learned from，是典型推断题信号。","拆句：It can be learned from the last paragraph that tipping ________. It 为形式主语，that 引 导真正主语从句 tipping ________；从句主语 tipping 后接空缺谓语（由选项补全）；can be learned from 是被动情态结构，提示答案是引申而非原文照搬。","定位：However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often. And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality. 然而许多顾客感到沮丧，因为他们觉得自己被要求支付太高的小费、还过于频繁。而且，正 如我们的研究所强调的，小费如今似乎更具强制性、更少出于慷慨，且常常与服务质量完全 脱钩。"]

questions.source_quote: However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often. And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality.

questions.content: According to the first two paragraphs, the NHS ________.
questions.options_json: {"A": "is troubled by funding deficiencies", "B": "can hardly satisfy people's needs", "C": "can barely retain its current employees", "D": "is rivalled by private medical services"}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"is troubled by funding deficiencies 用 funding deficiencies (资金短缺) 替换\"难以满 足需求\"，前两段未把矛头指向资金不足，只说成本挤压其他公共服务投入。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible ↔ can hardly satisfy people's needs model is out of date ↔ can hardly satisfy people's needs 预判\"需求难被满足\"与 can hardly satisfy people's needs 完全同义，直接锁 B。"},"C":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"can barely retain its current employees 把 pressures on the workforce 偷换成\"留 不住员工\"，原文只说人员压力大，并未谈\"留不住/流失\"。"},"D":{"trapType":"过度推断","explanation":"is rivalled by private medical services 暗示 NHS 受私营医疗的竞争挑战，原文 pay for private treatment 只是说没钱付私营治疗的人就医难，而非\"NHS 被私营对手 击败\"。"}}

questions.content: One answer to the crisis in health and care is to ________.

questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文从未提到 \"列车调度复杂\" 是中断原因；Complex train schedules 利用 the situation becomes highly complex 中的 complex 一词制造熟词错觉，但 highly complex 修饰的是 situation（局面），不是 schedules（时刻表）。"},"B":{"trapType":"与原文相反","explanation":"原文 planned investments of €24bn by 2026 与 €124bn in infrastructure over the next 10 years 显示投资规模庞大；Shortage of investments 称 \"投资不足\"，与原文 相反。"},"C":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"lack of capacity ↔ Its limited capacity there is no spare capacity ↔ Its limited capacity 预判 \"容量不足\" 与 Its limited capacity 字面贴合，且原文 But lack of capacity is another problem 用 another 明确把它列为原因之一，与 one cause 的 one 完全 对应。"},"D":{"trapType":"无中生有","explanation":"原文从未把 \"铁路网规模庞大\" 列为中断原因；Its massive scale 利用 €124bn、 Naples, Bologna, Florence and Turin 等规模意象，把 \"规模大\" 推断为 \"导致中断\"， 但原文没有这一因果链。"}}

questions.steps_json: ["判型：Improvements to the Italian train network will include 直接问改进措施包括什么，是对 具体内容的事实询问，无推断信号。","拆句：Q35 是不完整陈述句，主语 Improvements to the Italian train network，谓语 will include 等待选项补全宾语；结构平铺无陷阱，但 will 的将来时与文末两段的前瞻表述需要 对齐。","定位：Improvements will also come from the high-density technology and satellite signalling that RFI has been investing in for years, say experts. questions.content: The author holds that the future of street festivals depends on ____
questions.options_json: {"A": "the variety of activities.", "B": "the generosity of attendants.", "C": "the reputation of neighborhoods.", "D": "the management of expenditures."}
questions.analysis_json: {"A":{"trapType":"以偏概全","explanation":"P5 虽出现 live indie music, local art, small business vendors 一类多种内容，但原文 并未把节日的存续归因于「活动种类多样」；the variety of activities 把局部描述当成 命运决定因素。"},"B":{"trapType":"正确","explanation":"they exist because of community support ↔ the generosity of attendants it happens when we all chip in ↔ the generosity of attendants gate donations reached their lowest point in our history ↔ the generosity of attendants 在四个选项中，只有 B 同时覆盖了 P2、P5 的「捐款下滑」与 P6 的「community support / chip in」呼吁；其他选项只对应局部、或与文意不符。"},"C":{"trapType":"答非所问","explanation":"原文谈 Hyde Park、Wicker Park 等社区名声，是为了说明节日扎根社区，并非把节日 存续归因于「社区名声」；the reputation of neighborhoods 与「未来取决于什么」 错位。"},"D":{"trapType":"偷换概念","explanation":"P5 提到 making additional cuts to reduce our costs 是被迫削减支出，但原文从未说 节日未来取决于「支出管理」；the management of expenditures 把「不得已的削 减」偷换成「靠管钱解决问题」。"}}
questions.steps_json: ["判型：The author holds that the future of street festivals depends on ____ 既不限段落、又问 作者主张，本质上是问全文主旨/作者最核心呼吁。","拆句：The author holds that the future of street festivals depends on ____ 是「主语 + holds that + 宾语从句」，宾语从句的谓语是 depends on，横线处补宾语；句式干净，需注意 depends on 与选项的搭配（介词 on 后须是名词性短语）。"]
